2.2.d: गार्हपत्याद् अविच्छिन्नाम् उदक धाराम् हरेत् तन्तुम् तन्वन् रजसो भानुमन् विहि इत्य् आहवनीयात् ।
2.2.m: From the Gārhapatya he should carry an unbroken stream of water up to the Āhavanīya, with: 'Stretching the warp, follow the light of the middle realm...'.

2.2.s: paścād gārhapatyasya upaviśya udann aṅgārān apohet suhutakṛtaḥ stha suhutam kariṣyatha iti |
2.2.d: पश्चाद् गार्हपत्यस्य उपविश्य उदन्न् अङ्गारान् अपोहेत् सुहुतकृतः स्थ सुहुतम् करिष्यथ इति ।
2.2.m: Having sat down to the west of the Gārhapatya, he should push out embers towards the north, with: 'You are makers of good offerings; you will make a good offering.'

2.2.s: teṣv agnihotram adhiśrayed adhiśritam adhyadhiśritam adhiśritam him iti |
2.2.d: तेष्व् अग्निहोत्रम् अधिश्रयेद् अधिश्रितम् अध्यधिश्रितम् अधिश्रितम् हिम् इति ।
2.2.m: Upon them he should place the Agnihotra offering on the fire, with: 'Placed on the fire; placed right on the fire; placed on the fire, him.'

2.2.s: iḷāyās padam ghṛtavac cara acaram jāta vedo havir idam juṣasva ye grāmyāḥ paśavo viśva rūpās teṣām saptānām mayi puṣṭir astv iti vā |
2.2.d: इऌआयास् पदम् घृतवच् चर अचरम् जात वेदो हविर् इदम् जुषस्व ये ग्राम्याः पशवो विश्व रूपास् तेषाम् सप्तानाम् मयि पुष्टिर् अस्त्व् इति वा ।
2.2.m: Or with: 'The footstep of Iḷā, rich in ghee, moving and unmoving, O Jātavedas, enjoy this oblation! Whatever domestic animals of all forms there are, of those seven let there be nourishment in me.'

2.2.s: na dadhy adhiśrayed adhiśrayed ity eke |
2.2.d: न दध्य् अधिश्रयेद् अधिश्रयेद् इत्य् एके ।
2.2.m: He should not place curd on the fire; 'he should place it on the fire,' say some.

2.3.s: payasā nitya homaḥ |
2.3.d: पयसा नित्य होमः ।
2.3.m: The regular offering is with milk.

2.3.s: yavāgūr odano dadhi sarpir grāma kāma anna adya kāma indriya kāma tejas kāmānām |
2.3.d: यवागूर् ओदनो दधि सर्पिर् ग्राम काम अन्न अद्य काम इन्द्रिय काम तेजस् कामानाम् ।
2.3.m: Barley gruel, boiled rice, curd, and clarified butter are for those desiring a village, desiring food, desiring vigor of the senses, and desiring fiery energy [respectively].

2.3.s: adhiśritam avajvalayet |
2.3.d: अधिश्रितम् अवज्वलयेत् ।
2.3.m: He should illuminate that which has been placed on the fire with a burning stick.

2.3.s: anadhiśrayam dadhy agniṣ ṭe tejo mā hārṣīr iti |
2.3.d: अनधिश्रयम् दध्य् अग्निष् टे तेजो मा हार्षीर् इति ।
2.3.m: When curd is not placed on the fire, [he illuminates it] with: 'Agni, let not your heat carry away [its] energy.'

2.3.s: sruveṇa pratiṣiñcyān na vā śāntir asy amṛtam asi iti |
2.3.d: स्रुवेण प्रतिषिञ्च्यान् न वा शान्तिर् अस्य् अमृतम् असि इति ।
2.3.m: He should pour [water] into it with the offering ladle, or not, with: 'You are pacification; you are nectar.'

2.3.s: tayor avyaticāraḥ |
2.3.d: तयोर् अव्यतिचारः ।
2.3.m: There is no transgression regarding either of the two [options].

2.3.s: punar jvalatā pariharet trir antaritam rakṣo antaritā arātaya iti |
2.3.d: पुनर् ज्वलता परिहरेत् त्रिर् अन्तरितम् रक्षो अन्तरिता अरातय इति ।
2.3.m: He should circle it three times with a flaming [stick], with: 'Kept away is the demon; kept away are the enemies.'

2.3.s: samudantam karṣann iva udann udvāsayed dive tvā antarikṣāya tvā pṛthivyai tvā iti nidadhat |
2.3.d: समुदन्तम् कर्षन्न् इव उदन्न् उद्वासयेद् दिवे त्वा अन्तरिक्षाय त्वा पृथिव्यै त्वा इति निदधत् ।
2.3.m: As if scraping along the surface of the water, he should take it down towards the north, setting it down with: 'To heaven you! To the atmosphere you! To the earth you!'

2.3.s: suhuta kṛtaḥ stha suhutam akārṣṭa ity aṅgārān atisṛjya sruk sruvam pratitapet pratyuṣṭam rakṣaḥ pratyuṣṭā arātayo niṣṭaptam rakṣo niṣṭaptā arātaya iti |
2.3.d: सुहुत कृतः स्थ सुहुतम् अकार्ष्ट इत्य् अङ्गारान् अतिसृज्य स्रुक् स्रुवम् प्रतितपेत् प्रत्युष्टम् रक्षः प्रत्युष्टा अरातयो निष्टप्तम् रक्षो निष्टप्ता अरातय इति ।
2.3.m: Having pushed back the embers with: 'You are makers of good offerings; you made a good offering,' he should warm the offering ladle and the dipping spoon over the fire, with: 'Scorched away is the demon, scorched away the enemies! Burnt away is the demon, burnt away the enemies!'

2.3.s: uttarataḥ sthālyāḥ sruvam āsādya om unnayāni ity atisarjayīta |
2.3.d: उत्तरतः स्थाल्याः स्रुवम् आसाद्य ओम् उन्नयानि इत्य् अतिसर्जयीत ।
2.3.m: Having placed the dipping spoon to the north of the pot, he should seek permission, saying: 'Om, may I ladle out?'

2.3.s: āhita agnir ācamya apareṇa vedim ativrajya dakṣiṇata upaviśya etat śrutvā om unnaya ity atisṛjet |
2.3.d: आहित अग्निर् आचम्य अपरेण वेदिम् अतिव्रज्य दक्षिणत उपविश्य एतत् श्रुत्वा ओम् उन्नय इत्य् अतिसृजेत् ।
2.3.m: The one who has established the sacred fires, having rinsed his mouth, passed behind the vedi, and sat to the south, upon hearing this, gives permission, saying: 'Om, ladle out!'

2.3.s: atisṛṣo bhūr iḷā bhuva iḷā svar iḷā vṛdha iḷā iti sruva pūram unnayet |
2.3.d: अतिसृषो भूर् इऌआ भुव इऌआ स्वर् इऌआ वृध इऌआ इति स्रुव पूरम् उन्नयेत् ।
2.3.m: Having been permitted, he should ladle out spoonfuls [of oblation], with: 'Bhūr Iḷā! Bhuvar Iḷā! Svar Iḷā! Vṛdhar Iḷā!'

2.3.s: agniyam agniyam pūrṇatamam yo anu jyeṣṭham ṛddhim icchet putrāṇām |
2.3.d: अग्नियम् अग्नियम् पूर्णतमम् यो अनु ज्येष्ठम् ऋद्धिम् इच्छेत् पुत्राणाम् ।
2.3.m: Each subsequent one fuller, if he desires the eldest of his sons to prosper in succession.

2.3.s: yo asya putraḥ priyaḥ syāt tam prati pūrṇam unnayet |
2.3.d: यो अस्य पुत्रः प्रियः स्यात् तम् प्रति पूर्णम् उन्नयेत् ।
2.3.m: Whichever son is dear to him, for his sake he should ladle it out full.

2.3.s: sthālīm abhimṛśya samidham srucam ca adhy adhi gārhapatyam hṛtvā prāṇa sammitām āhavanīya samīpe kuśeṣu upasādya jān ācya samidham ādadhyād rajatām tvā agni jyotiṣam rātrim iṣṭakām upadadhe svāhā iti |
2.3.d: स्थालीम् अभिमृश्य समिधम् स्रुचम् च अध्य् अधि गार्हपत्यम् हृत्वा प्राण सम्मिताम् आहवनीय समीपे कुशेषु उपसाद्य जान् आच्य समिधम् आदध्याद् रजताम् त्वा अग्नि ज्योतिषम् रात्रिम् इष्टकाम् उपदधे स्वाहा इति ।
2.3.m: Having touched the pot, taken the kindling stick and the offering ladle directly over the Gārhapatya fire, held at the level of his breath, set them down near the Āhavanīya upon kuśa grass, and bent his knee, he should place the kindling stick [on the fire], with: 'You, the silver brick, the night, having Agni as light, I place; svāhā!'

2.3.s: samidham ādhāya vidyud asi vidya me pāpmānam agnau śraddhā ity apa upaspṛśya pradīptām dvy aṅgula mātre abhijuhuyād bhūr bhuvaḥ svar om agnir jyotir jyotir agniḥ svāhā iti |
2.3.d: समिधम् आधाय विद्युद् असि विद्य मे पाप्मानम् अग्नौ श्रद्धा इत्य् अप उपस्पृश्य प्रदीप्ताम् द्व्य् अङ्गुल मात्रे अभिजुहुयाद् भूर् भुवः स्वर् ओम् अग्निर् ज्योतिर् ज्योतिर् अग्निः स्वाहा इति ।
2.3.m: Having placed the kindling stick, touched water with: 'You are lightning; cut off my sin! In Agni is faith!', he should make the offering directly onto the blaze at a distance of two finger-breadths, with: 'Bhūr bhuvaḥ svar, Om! Agni is light, light is Agni, svāhā!'

2.3.s: pūrvām āhutim hutvā kuśeṣu sādayitvā gārhapatyam eva īkṣeta paśūn me yaccha iti |
2.3.d: पूर्वाम् आहुतिम् हुत्वा कुशेषु सादयित्वा गार्हपत्यम् एव ईक्षेत पशून् मे यच्छ इति ।
2.3.m: Having made the first offering and set [the ladle] down upon kuśa grass, he should look directly at the Gārhapatya fire, saying: 'Grant me cattle.'

2.3.s: atha uttarām tūṣṇīm bhūyasīm asaṃsṛṣṭām prāg udag uttarato vā |
2.3.d: अथ उत्तराम् तूष्णीम् भूयसीम् असंसृष्टाम् प्राग् उदग् उत्तरतो वा ।
2.3.m: Then the second [offering], in silence, larger, not in contact [with the first], towards the northeast or north.

2.3.s: prajāpatim manasā dhyāyāt tūṣṇīm homeṣu sarvatra |
2.3.d: प्रजापतिम् मनसा ध्यायात् तूष्णीम् होमेषु सर्वत्र ।
2.3.m: He should meditate on Prajāpati with the mind, everywhere in silent offerings.

2.3.s: bhūyiṣṭham sruci śiṣṭvā trir anuprakampya avamṛjya kuśa mūleṣu nimārṣṭi paśubhyas tvā iti |
2.3.d: भूयिष्ठम् स्रुचि शिष्ट्वा त्रिर् अनुप्रकम्प्य अवमृज्य कुश मूलेषु निमार्ष्टि पशुभ्यस् त्वा इति ।
2.3.m: Having left the greater part in the ladle, shaken it three times, and wiped it downwards, he wipes it clean on the roots of the kuśa grass, with: 'To the cattle you!'

2.3.s: teṣām dakṣiṇata uttānā aṅgulīḥ karoti prācīna āvītī tūṣṇīm svadhā pitṛbhya iti vā |
2.3.d: तेषाम् दक्षिणत उत्ताना अङ्गुलीः करोति प्राचीन आवीती तूष्णीम् स्वधा पितृभ्य इति वा ।
2.3.m: To the south of them, wearing the sacred cord over the right shoulder, he holds his fingers turned upwards, in silence, or with: 'Svadhā to the fathers!'

2.3.s: apo avaninīya |
2.3.d: अपो अवनिनीय ।

2.3.s: vṛṣṭir asi vṛśca me pāpmānam apsu śraddhā ity apa upaspṛśya |
2.3.d: वृष्टिर् असि वृश्च मे पाप्मानम् अप्सु श्रद्धा इत्य् अप उपस्पृश्य ।
2.3.m: and touched water with: 'You are rain; cut off my sin! In the waters is faith!',

2.3.s: āhita agnir anumantrayeta |
2.3.d: आहित अग्निर् अनुमन्त्रयेत ।
2.3.m: the one who has established the sacred fires should follow with recitation.

2.3.s: ādhānam uktvā tena ṛṣiṇā tena brahmaṇā tayā devatayā aṅgirasvad dhruvā āsīda iti samidham |
2.3.d: आधानम् उक्त्वा तेन ऋषिणा तेन ब्रह्मणा तया देवतया अङ्गिरस्वद् ध्रुवा आसीद इति समिधम् ।
2.3.m: Having recited the placing [formula], he follows the kindling stick with: 'With that seer, with that sacred formulation, with that deity, like Aṅgiras, sit firm.'

2.3.s: tā asya sūda dohasa iti pūrvām āhutim |
2.3.d: ता अस्य सूद दोहस इति पूर्वाम् आहुतिम् ।
2.3.m: He follows the first offering with: 'Those milkings of his...'.

2.3.s: upasthāya uttarām kāṃkṣeta īkṣamāṇo bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ suprajāḥ prajābhiḥ syām suvīro vīraiḥ supoṣaḥ poṣaiḥ |
2.3.d: उपस्थाय उत्तराम् कांक्षेत ईक्षमाणो भूर् भुवः स्वः सुप्रजाः प्रजाभिः स्याम् सुवीरो वीरैः सुपोषः पोषैः ।
2.3.m: Having stood up before [the fire], looking at it, he should await the second [offering], with: 'Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! May I have good offspring through offspring, be rich in heroic sons through heroic sons, rich in nourishment through nourishment!'

2.3.s: āgneyībhiś ca |
2.3.d: आग्नेयीभिश् च ।

2.3.s: agna āyūṃṣi pavasa iti tisṛbhiḥ |
2.3.d: अग्न आयूंषि पवस इति तिसृभिः ।
2.3.m: with the three [verses beginning]: 'O Agni, you purify our life-spans...'.

2.4.s: yavāgvā payasā vā svayam parvaṇi juhuyāt |
2.4.d: यवाग्वा पयसा वा स्वयम् पर्वणि जुहुयात् ।
2.4.m: he should make the offering himself on the junction day of the moon, with barley gruel or with milk.
One of the officiating priests [offers] at other times,
Having touched water and turned towards the north, he should consume [the remainder].

2.4.s: āyuṣe tvā prāśnāmi iti prathamam | anna adyāya tvā ity uttaram |
2.4.d: आयुषे त्वा प्राश्नामि इति प्रथमम् । अन्न अद्याय त्वा इत्य् उत्तरम् ।
2.4.m: 'I consume you for long life,' is the first [formula]; 'For food,' is the next.

2.4.s: tūṣṇīm samidham ādhāya agnaye gṛhapataye svāhā iti gārhapatye |
2.4.d: तूष्णीम् समिधम् आधाय अग्नये गृहपतये स्वाहा इति गार्हपत्ये ।
2.4.m: Having placed a kindling stick in silence, [he offers] in the Gārhapatya, with: 'To Agni, lord of the house, svāhā!'

2.4.s: tūṣṇīm samidham ādhāya agnaye saṃveśa pataye svāhā iti dakṣiṇe | agnaye annādāya anna pataye svāhā iti vā |
2.4.d: तूष्णीम् समिधम् आधाय अग्नये संवेश पतये स्वाहा इति दक्षिणे । अग्नये अन्नादाय अन्न पतये स्वाहा इति वा ।
2.4.m: Having placed a kindling stick in silence, [he offers] in the Dakṣiṇa fire, with: 'To Agni, lord of resting, svāhā!' or 'To Agni, the eater of food, the lord of food, svāhā!'

2.4.s: atha enām kuśaiḥ prakṣālya catasraḥ pūrṇāḥ prāg udīcyor ninayed ṛtubhyaḥ svāhā digbhyaḥ svāhā saptarṣibhyaḥ svāhā itara janebhyaḥ svāhā iti |
2.4.d: अथ एनाम् कुशैः प्रक्षाल्य चतस्रः पूर्णाः प्राग् उदीच्योर् निनयेद् ऋतुभ्यः स्वाहा दिग्भ्यः स्वाहा सप्तर्षिभ्यः स्वाहा इतर जनेभ्यः स्वाहा इति ।
2.4.m: Then, having washed it with kuśa blades, he should pour out four full [spoonfuls of water] towards the northeast, with: 'To the seasons, svāhā! To the directions, svāhā! To the Seven Seers, svāhā! To the other people, svāhā!'

2.4.s: pañcamīm kuśa deśe pṛthivyām amṛtam juhomy agnaye vaiśvānarāya svāhā iti | ṣaṣṭhīm paścād gārhapatyasya prāṇam amṛte juhomy amṛtam prāṇe juhomi svāhā iti |
2.4.d: पञ्चमीम् कुश देशे पृथिव्याम् अमृतम् जुहोम्य् अग्नये वैश्वानराय स्वाहा इति । षष्ठीम् पश्चाद् गार्हपत्यस्य प्राणम् अमृते जुहोम्य् अमृतम् प्राणे जुहोमि स्वाहा इति ।
2.4.m: The fifth on the spot of kuśa grass, with: 'On the earth I offer nectar to Agni Vaiśvānara, svāhā!'; the sixth behind the Gārhapatya, with: 'I offer breath into nectar; I offer nectar into breath, svāhā!'
Having heated [the ladle], he should place it inside the vedi.
He should hand it over to the attendant.

2.4.s: agreṇa āhavanīyam parītya samidha ādadhyāt tisras tisra udan mukhas tiṣṭhan |
2.4.d: अग्रेण आहवनीयम् परीत्य समिध आदध्यात् तिस्रस् तिस्र उदन् मुखस् तिष्ठन् ।
2.4.m: Having gone around in front of the Āhavanīya fire, standing facing north, he should place three kindling sticks on each [fire],
the first accompanied by a sacred formula.

2.4.s: āhavanīye dīdihi iti gārhapatye dīdāya iti dakṣiṇe dīdidāya iti |
2.4.d: आहवनीये दीदिहि इति गार्हपत्ये दीदाय इति दक्षिणे दीदिदाय इति ।
2.4.m: On the Āhavanīya with 'shine forth (dīdihi)', on the Gārhapatya with 'shining (dīdāya)', on the Dakṣiṇa with 'shone forth (dīdidāya)'.
The sprinkling with water has been explained.
With those two [formulas, the two] sweeping-rounds [are performed].
The first two, however, before the sprinkling with water.
At daybreak, at dawn, or when [the sun] has risen.

2.4.s: satya ṛtābhyām tvā iti paryukṣaṇam om unneṣyāmi ity atisarjanam hariṇīm tvā sūrya jyotiṣam ahar iṣṭakām upadadhe svāhā iti samid ādhānam bhūr bhuvaḥ svar om sūryo jyotir jyotiḥ sūryaḥ svāhā iti homa unmārjanam ca |
2.4.d: सत्य ऋताभ्याम् त्वा इति पर्युक्षणम् ओम् उन्नेष्यामि इत्य् अतिसर्जनम् हरिणीम् त्वा सूर्य ज्योतिषम् अहर् इष्टकाम् उपदधे स्वाहा इति समिद् आधानम् भूर् भुवः स्वर् ओम् सूर्यो ज्योतिर् ज्योतिः सूर्यः स्वाहा इति होम उन्मार्जनम् च ।
2.4.m: The sprinkling with water is with 'Thee with truth and cosmic order'; the permission is with 'Om, I will take out'; the laying of fuel is with 'Thee the yellow one, having the sun's light, day-brick, I lay down, svāhā'; the offering and the wiping are with 'Bhūr bhuvaḥ svar om, Sūrya is light, the light is Sūrya, svāhā'.

2.5.s: pravatsyann agnīn prajvalya ācamya atikramya upatiṣṭhate |
2.5.d: प्रवत्स्यन्न् अग्नीन् प्रज्वल्य आचम्य अतिक्रम्य उपतिष्ठते ।
2.5.m: When about to set out on a journey, having made the fires blaze up, having sipped water, and having stepped forward, he attends upon [the fires].

2.5.s: āhavanīyam śaṃsya paśūn me pāhi iti | gārhapatyam naya prajām me pāhi iti | dakṣiṇam atharva pitum me pāhi iti | gārhapatya āhavanīyāv īkṣeta imān me mitrā varuṇau gṛhān gopāyatam yuvam avinaṣṭān avihṛtān pūṣā enān abhirakṣatv asmākam punar ā ayanād iti |
2.5.d: आहवनीयम् शंस्य पशून् मे पाहि इति । गार्हपत्यम् नय प्रजाम् मे पाहि इति । दक्षिणम् अथर्व पितुम् मे पाहि इति । गार्हपत्य आहवनीयाव् ईक्षेत इमान् मे मित्रा वरुणौ गृहान् गोपायतम् युवम् अविनष्टान् अविहृतान् पूषा एनान् अभिरक्षत्व् अस्माकम् पुनर् आ अयनाद् इति ।
2.5.m: [He attends upon] the Āhavanīya with 'O praiseworthy one, protect my cattle'; the Gārhapatya with 'O leader, protect my offspring'; the Dakṣiṇa with 'O Atharvan, protect my food'. He should look at the Gārhapatya and Āhavanīya fires with 'O Mitra and Varuṇa, do ye two protect these homes of mine, undestroyed, unscattered; let Pūṣan guard them until our return'.

2.5.s: yathā pratyetya pradakṣiṇam paryann āhavanīyam upatiṣṭhate | mama nāma prathamam jāta vedaḥ pitā mātā ca dadhatur yad agne | tattvam bibhṛhi punar ā mama etos tava aham nāma bibharāṇy agra iti |
2.5.d: यथा प्रत्येत्य प्रदक्षिणम् पर्यन्न् आहवनीयम् उपतिष्ठते । मम नाम प्रथमम् जात वेदः पिता माता च दधतुर् यद् अग्ने । तत्त्वम् बिभृहि पुनर् आ मम एतोस् तव अहम् नाम बिभराण्य् अग्र इति ।
2.5.m: Having returned the way he came, circumambulating clockwise, he attends upon the Āhavanīya fire with 'My first name, O Jātavedas, which father and mother gave [me], O Agni, that do thou bear until my return; I will bear thy name, O Agni'.

2.5.s: pravrajed anavekṣamāṇo mā praṇama iti sūktam japan |
2.5.d: प्रव्रजेद् अनवेक्षमाणो मा प्रणम इति सूक्तम् जपन् ।
2.5.m: He should set forth without looking back, muttering the hymn 'Do not bend away'.
Far from the fires, he should release his speech.

2.5.s: sadā sugaḥ pitur mā astu panthā iti panthānam avaruhya |
2.5.d: सदा सुगः पितुर् मा अस्तु पन्था इति पन्थानम् अवरुह्य ।
2.5.m: Having descended upon the path with 'May the path of the father always be easy for me to travel'.

2.5.s: anupasthita agniś cet pravāsam āpadyeta | iha eva san tatra santam tvā agne hṛdā vācā manasā vā bibharmi | tiro mā santam mā prahāsīr jyotiṣā tvā vaiśvānareṇa upatiṣṭhata iti pratidiśam agnīn upasthāya |
2.5.d: अनुपस्थित अग्निश् चेत् प्रवासम् आपद्येत । इह एव सन् तत्र सन्तम् त्वा अग्ने हृदा वाचा मनसा वा बिभर्मि । तिरो मा सन्तम् मा प्रहासीर् ज्योतिषा त्वा वैश्वानरेण उपतिष्ठत इति प्रतिदिशम् अग्नीन् उपस्थाय ।
2.5.m: If he should start on a journey without having attended upon the fires, having attended upon the fires facing each direction with 'Being right here, thee who art there, O Agni, I hold with heart, speech, or mind; do not abandon me who am away; I attend upon thee with Vaiśvānara light'.
Having returned with 'We have entered upon the path'.

2.5.s: sami pāṇir vāg yato agnīn jvalataḥ śrutvā abhikramya āhavanīyam īkṣeta | viśvadānīm ābharanto anātureṇa manasā | agne mā te prativeśā riṣāma | namas te astu mīḷhuṣe namas ta upasadvane | agne śumbhasva tanvaḥ sam mā rayyā sṛja iti |
2.5.d: समि पाणिर् वाग् यतो अग्नीन् ज्वलतः श्रुत्वा अभिक्रम्य आहवनीयम् ईक्षेत । विश्वदानीम् आभरन्तो अनातुरेण मनसा । अग्ने मा ते प्रतिवेशा रिषाम । नमस् ते अस्तु मीऌहुषे नमस् त उपसद्वने । अग्ने शुम्भस्व तन्वः सम् मा रय्या सृज इति ।
2.5.m: With fuel in hand, restraining his speech, having heard that the fires are blazing, having stepped forward, he should look at the Āhavanīya fire with 'Bringing [homage] at all times with an untroubled mind, O Agni, may we thy neighbors not suffer harm. Homage be to thee, the bounteous one; homage to thee who art approached. O Agni, adorn thy bodies; unite me with wealth'.

2.5.s: agniṣu samidha upanidhāya āhavanīyam upatiṣṭhate | mama nāma tava ca jāta vedo vāsasī iva vivasānau carāvaḥ | te bibhṛvo dakṣase jīvase ca yathā yatham nau tanvā jāta veda iti |
2.5.d: अग्निषु समिध उपनिधाय आहवनीयम् उपतिष्ठते । मम नाम तव च जात वेदो वाससी इव विवसानौ चरावः । ते बिभृवो दक्षसे जीवसे च यथा यथम् नौ तन्वा जात वेद इति ।
2.5.m: Having laid down fuel near the fires, he attends upon the Āhavanīya fire with 'My name and thine, O Jātavedas, let us two move wearing them like garments; let us two bear them for capability and for life, each in our proper body, O Jātavedas'.
Then he should lay the fuel sticks on [the fires].

2.5.s: āhavanīye agnama viśva vedasam asmabhyam vasuvittamam | agne saṃrāḷ abhidyumnam abhisaha āyacchasva svāhā iti | gārhapatye ayam agnir gṛha patir gārhapatyaḥ prajāyā vasuvittamaḥ | agne gṛhapate abhidyumnam abhisaha āyacchasva svāhā iti | dakṣiṇe ayam agniḥ purīṣyo rayimān puṣṭi vardhanaḥ | agne purīṣya abhidyumnam abhisaha āyacchasva svāhā iti | gārhapatya āhavanīyāv īkṣeta imān me mitrā varuṇau gṛhān ajūgupatam yuvam | avinaṣṭān avihṛtān pūṣā enān abhyārakṣīd asmākam punar ā ayanād iti |
2.5.d: आहवनीये अग्नम विश्व वेदसम् अस्मभ्यम् वसुवित्तमम् । अग्ने संराऌ अभिद्युम्नम् अभिसह आयच्छस्व स्वाहा इति । गार्हपत्ये अयम् अग्निर् गृह पतिर् गार्हपत्यः प्रजाया वसुवित्तमः । अग्ने गृहपते अभिद्युम्नम् अभिसह आयच्छस्व स्वाहा इति । दक्षिणे अयम् अग्निः पुरीष्यो रयिमान् पुष्टि वर्धनः । अग्ने पुरीष्य अभिद्युम्नम् अभिसह आयच्छस्व स्वाहा इति । गार्हपत्य आहवनीयाव् ईक्षेत इमान् मे मित्रा वरुणौ गृहान् अजूगुपतम् युवम् । अविनष्टान् अविहृतान् पूषा एनान् अभ्यारक्षीद् अस्माकम् पुनर् आ अयनाद् इति ।
2.5.m:
On the Āhavanīya fire with 'Agni, the all-knowing, who finds wealth for us best, O sovereign Agni, extend glory and strength, svāhā'; on the Gārhapatya with 'This Agni, lord of the house, Gārhapatya, best finder of wealth for offspring, O Agni, lord of the house, extend glory and strength, svāhā'; on the Dakṣiṇa with 'This Agni, dwelling in the earth, possessing wealth, increaser of prosperity'.
'O Agni, dwelling in the earth, extend glory and strength, svāhā'. He should look at the Gārhapatya and Āhavanīya fires with 'O Mitra and Varuṇa, ye two have guarded these homes of mine, undestroyed, unscattered; Pūṣan has guarded them until our return'.

2.5.s: yathā itam pratyetya | parisamūhya udag vihārād upaviśya bhūr bhuvaḥ svar iti vācam visṛjet |
2.5.d: यथा इतम् प्रत्येत्य । परिसमूह्य उदग् विहाराद् उपविश्य भूर् भुवः स्वर् इति वाचम् विसृजेत् ।
2.5.m: Having returned the way he went, having swept round [the fires], and having sat down to the north of the sacrificial enclosure, he should release his speech with 'Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ'.

2.5.s: proṣya bhūyo daśarātrāc catur gṛhītam ājyam juhuyāt mano jyotir juṣatām ājyam me vicchinnam yajñam sam imam dadhātu | yā iṣṭā uṣaso yā aniṣṭās tāḥ saṃtanomi haviṣā ghṛtena svāhā iti |
2.5.d: प्रोष्य भूयो दशरात्राच् चतुर् गृहीतम् आज्यम् जुहुयात् मनो ज्योतिर् जुषताम् आज्यम् मे विच्छिन्नम् यज्ञम् सम् इमम् दधातु । या इष्टा उषसो या अनिष्टास् ताः संतनोमि हविषा घृतेन स्वाहा इति ।
2.5.m: Having stayed away for more than ten nights, he should offer four ladlings of clarified butter with 'May the mind-light enjoy my clarified butter; may it join together this disrupted sacrifice of mine; those dawns which have been sacrificed and those which have not, I unite them with the offering, with ghee, svāhā'.
And also in case of non-performance of the Agnihotra.

2.5.s: gṛhān īkṣeta apy anāhita agnir gṛhā mā bibhīta upamaḥ svastye vo asmāsu ca prajāyadhvam mā ca vo gopatī riṣad iti prapadyeta | gṛhān aham sumanasaḥ prapadye vīraghno vīravataḥ suvīrān | irām vahanto ghṛtam ukṣamāṇās teṣv aham sumanāḥ saṃviśāni iti śivam śagmam śamyoḥ śamyor iti trir anuvīkṣamāṇaḥ |
2.5.d: गृहान् ईक्षेत अप्य् अनाहित अग्निर् गृहा मा बिभीत उपमः स्वस्त्ये वो अस्मासु च प्रजायध्वम् मा च वो गोपती रिषद् इति प्रपद्येत । गृहान् अहम् सुमनसः प्रपद्ये वीरघ्नो वीरवतः सुवीरान् । इराम् वहन्तो घृतम् उक्षमाणास् तेष्व् अहम् सुमनाः संविशानि इति शिवम् शग्मम् शम्योः शम्योर् इति त्रिर् अनुवीक्षमाणः ।
2.5.m: Even one who has not established sacred fires should look at the houses and enter with 'O houses, fear me not; approach for our well-being and be fruitful among us, and may your master of cattle not suffer harm'; looking repeatedly thrice with 'I enter the well-disposed houses, which do not kill heroes, possess heroes, and have good heroes; carrying refreshing food, sprinkling ghee, in them may I dwell with a benevolent mind; auspicious, beneficial, peace and blessing, peace and blessing'.

2.5.s: viditam apy alīkam na tad ahar jñāpayeyuḥ |
2.5.d: विदितम् अप्य् अलीकम् न तद् अहर् ज्ञापयेयुः ।
2.5.m: Even if something unpleasant has occurred, they should not inform him on that day.

2.5.s: vijñāyate abhayam vo abhayam em astv ity eva upatiṣṭheta pravasan pratyetya ahar ahar vā iti |
2.5.d: विज्ञायते अभयम् वो अभयम् एम् अस्त्व् इत्य् एव उपतिष्ठेत प्रवसन् प्रत्येत्य अहर् अहर् वा इति ।
2.5.m: It is taught in the sacred text: 'He should attend with just "May there be safety for you, safety for me," when returning from a journey or day by day'.

2.6.s: amāvāsyāyām apara ahṇe piṇḍa pitṛ yajñaḥ |
2.6.d: अमावास्यायाम् अपर अह्णे पिण्ड पितृ यज्ञः ।
2.6.m: On the new-moon day, in the afternoon, [is] the ball-offering to the ancestors (Piṇḍapitṛyajña).

2.6.s: dakṣiṇa agner eka ulmukam prāg dakṣiṇā praṇayed ye rūpāṇi pratimuñcamānā asurāḥ santaḥ svadhayā caranti | parāpuro nipuro ye bharanty agniṣ ṭāṃl lokāt praṇudātv asmād iti |
2.6.d: दक्षिण अग्नेर् एक उल्मुकम् प्राग् दक्षिणा प्रणयेद् ये रूपाणि प्रतिमुञ्चमाना असुराः सन्तः स्वधया चरन्ति । परापुरो निपुरो ये भरन्त्य् अग्निष् टांल् लोकात् प्रणुदात्व् अस्माद् इति ।
2.6.m: From the Dakṣiṇa fire he should carry forward a single firebrand toward the south-east with 'The Asuras who, putting on forms, move about according to their own will, who carry away the distant and near strongholds, may Agni expel them from this world'.

2.6.s: sarva karmāṇi tām diśam |
2.6.d: सर्व कर्माणि ताम् दिशम् ।
2.6.m: All rites are [directed toward] that quarter.

2.6.s: upasamādhāya ubhau paristīrya dakṣiṇa agneḥ prāg udak pratyag udag vā eka ekaśaḥ pātrāṇi sādayec caru sthāli śūrpa sphya ulūkhala musala sruva dhruva kṛṣṇa ajina sakṛd ācchinna idhma mekṣaṇa kamaṇḍalūn |
2.6.d: उपसमाधाय उभौ परिस्तीर्य दक्षिण अग्नेः प्राग् उदक् प्रत्यग् उदग् वा एक एकशः पात्राणि सादयेच् चरु स्थालि शूर्प स्फ्य उलूखल मुसल स्रुव ध्रुव कृष्ण अजिन सकृद् आच्छिन्न इध्म मेक्षण कमण्डलून् ।
2.6.m: Having added fuel and having strewn grass around both [fires], he should place the utensils one by one to the north-east or north-west of the Dakṣiṇa fire: the cooking pot, winnowing basket, wooden sword, mortar, pestle, spoon, Dhruvā ladle, black antelope skin, fuel bundle cut once, stirring stick, and water jar.

2.6.s: dakṣiṇato agniṣṭham āruhya caru sthālīm vrīhīṇām pūrṇām nimṛjet |
2.6.d: दक्षिणतो अग्निष्ठम् आरुह्य चरु स्थालीम् व्रीहीणाम् पूर्णाम् निमृजेत् ।
2.6.m: Having mounted the cart from the south, he should wipe off the cooking pot full of rice grains.

2.6.s: pariśannān nidadhyāt |
2.6.d: परिशन्नान् निदध्यात् ।
2.6.m: He should put down those [grains] that have spilled around.

2.6.s: kṛṣṇa ajina ulūkhalam kṛtvā itarān patny avahanyād avivecam |
2.6.d: कृष्ण अजिन उलूखलम् कृत्वा इतरान् पत्न्य् अवहन्याद् अविवेचम् ।
2.6.m: Having placed the black antelope skin and the mortar, the wife should pound the rest without separating [them into halves].

2.6.s: avahatānt sakṛt prakṣālya dakṣiṇa agnau śrapayet |
2.6.d: अवहतान्त् सकृत् प्रक्षाल्य दक्षिण अग्नौ श्रपयेत् ।
2.6.m: Having washed the pounded [grains] once, he should cook them on the Dakṣiṇa fire.

2.6.s: arvāg atipraṇītāt sphyena lekhām ullikhed apahatā asurā rakṣāṃsi vediṣada iti |
2.6.d: अर्वाग् अतिप्रणीतात् स्फ्येन लेखाम् उल्लिखेद् अपहता असुरा रक्षांसि वेदिषद इति ।
2.6.m: On this side of the carried-forward firebrand, he should draw a line with the wooden sword, with 'Slain are the Asuras and the Rakṣases that sit on the altar'.

2.6.s: tām abhyukṣya sakṛd ācchinnair avastīrya āsādayed abhighārya sthālī pākam ājyam sarpir anutpūtam nava nītam vā utpūtam dhruvāyām ājyam kṛtvā dakṣiṇataḥ |
2.6.d: ताम् अभ्युक्ष्य सकृद् आच्छिन्नैर् अवस्तीर्य आसादयेद् अभिघार्य स्थाली पाकम् आज्यम् सर्पिर् अनुत्पूतम् नव नीतम् वा उत्पूतम् ध्रुवायाम् आज्यम् कृत्वा दक्षिणतः ।
2.6.m: Having sprinkled it with water and strewn it with [grass] cut in a single stroke, having poured clarified butter over the cooked pot-offering, he should place it down, and having made clarified butter, either clarified butter that is unpurified or purified butter, in the Dhruvā ladle, [place it] to the south.

2.6.s: āñjana abhyañjana kaśipu upabarhaṇāni |
2.6.d: आञ्जन अभ्यञ्जन कशिपु उपबर्हणानि ।
2.6.m: [And to the south he places] the eye-salve, body-ointment, cushion, and pillow.

2.6.s: prācīna āvītī idhmam upasamādhāya mekṣaṇena ādāya avadāna sampadā juhuyāt somāya pitṛmate svadhā namo agnaye kavya vāhanāya svadhā nama iti |
2.6.d: प्राचीन आवीती इध्मम् उपसमाधाय मेक्षणेन आदाय अवदान सम्पदा जुहुयात् सोमाय पितृमते स्वधा नमो अग्नये कव्य वाहनाय स्वधा नम इति ।
2.6.m: Wearing the sacred cord over the right shoulder, having placed the fuel bundle upon the fire, having scooped [a portion of the cooked mess] with the stirring-stick according to the rule of cuttings, he should make an oblation with: 'To Soma accompanied by the ancestors, svadhā! Reverence! To Agni the bearer of funeral offerings, svadhā! Reverence!'

2.6.s: svāhā kāreṇa vā agnim pūrvam yajña upavītī |
2.6.d: स्वाहा कारेण वा अग्निम् पूर्वम् यज्ञ उपवीती ।
2.6.m: Or wearing the sacred cord over the left shoulder, [he should offer] to Agni first, with the exclamation svāhā.

2.6.s: mekṣaṇam anuprahṛtya prācīna āvītī lekhām trir udakena upanayet śundhantām pitaraḥ śundhantām pitāmahāḥ śundhantām prapitāmahā iti |
2.6.d: मेक्षणम् अनुप्रहृत्य प्राचीन आवीती लेखाम् त्रिर् उदकेन उपनयेत् शुन्धन्ताम् पितरः शुन्धन्ताम् पितामहाः शुन्धन्ताम् प्रपितामहा इति ।
2.6.m: Having thrown the stirring-stick after [into the fire], wearing the sacred cord over the right shoulder, he should trace out the line three times with water [saying]: 'May the fathers be purified! May the grandfathers be purified! May the great-grandfathers be purified!'

2.6.s: tasyām piṇḍān nipṛṇīyāt parācīna pāṇiḥ pitre pitāmahāya prapitāmahāya etat te asau ye ca tvām atra anv iti |
2.6.d: तस्याम् पिण्डान् निपृणीयात् पराचीन पाणिः पित्रे पितामहाय प्रपितामहाय एतत् ते असौ ये च त्वाम् अत्र अन्व् इति ।
2.6.m: On it he should present the rice balls, with the palm of his hand turned downwards, [saying]: 'For the father, for the grandfather, for the great-grandfather: this for you, so-and-so, and for those who follow you here.'

2.6.s: tasmai tasmai ya eṣām pretāḥ syur iti gāṇagāriḥ pratyakṣam itarān arcayet tad arthatvāt |
2.6.d: तस्मै तस्मै य एषाम् प्रेताः स्युर् इति गाणगारिः प्रत्यक्षम् इतरान् अर्चयेत् तद् अर्थत्वात् ।
2.6.m: 'For whichever of them may be deceased,' says Gāṇagāri; 'he should venerate the others visibly [in person], because that is the purpose.'

2.6.s: sarvebhya eva nipṛṇīyād iti tailvaliḥ kriyā guṇatvāt |
2.6.d: सर्वेभ्य एव निपृणीयाद् इति तैल्वलिः क्रिया गुणत्वात् ।
2.6.m: 'He should present [balls] to all of them without exception,' says Tailvali, 'because [the action] has the rite itself as its primary element.'

2.6.s: api jīva anta ā tribhyaḥ pretebhya eva nipṛṇīyād iti gautamaḥ kriyā hy artha kāritā |
2.6.d: अपि जीव अन्त आ त्रिभ्यः प्रेतेभ्य एव निपृणीयाद् इति गौतमः क्रिया ह्य् अर्थ कारिता ।
2.6.m: 'Even if [the line] ends with a living one, he should present [balls] only to the deceased, up to three,' says Gautama, 'for the ritual action is motivated by its purpose.'

2.6.s: upāya viśeṣo jīva mṛtānām |
2.6.d: उपाय विशेषो जीव मृतानाम् ।
2.6.m: There is a different method for the living and the dead.

2.6.s: na parebhyo anadhikārāt | na pratyakṣam | na jīvebhyo nipṛṇīyāt |
2.6.d: न परेभ्यो अनधिकारात् । न प्रत्यक्षम् । न जीवेभ्यो निपृणीयात् ।
2.6.m: Not to further ancestors, because there is no entitlement; not in visible person; he should not present balls to living persons.

2.6.s: na jīva antarhitebhyaḥ |
2.6.d: न जीव अन्तर्हितेभ्यः ।
2.6.m: Not to ancestors separated by a living person.

2.6.s: juhuyāj jīvebhyaḥ |
2.6.d: जुहुयाज् जीवेभ्यः ।
2.6.m: He should offer into the fire for the living.

2.6.s: sarva hutam sarva jīvinaḥ |
2.6.d: सर्व हुतम् सर्व जीविनः ।
2.6.m: He whose [ancestors] are all living offers everything into the fire.

2.6.s: nāmāny avidvāṃs tata pitāmaha prapitāmaha iti |
2.6.d: नामान्य् अविद्वांस् तत पितामह प्रपितामह इति ।
2.6.m: If he does not know their names, [he says]: 'O father, O grandfather, O great-grandfather.'

2.7.s: nipṛtān anumantrayeta atra pitaro mādayadhvam yathā bhāgam āvṛṣāyadhvam iti |
2.7.d: निपृतान् अनुमन्त्रयेत अत्र पितरो मादयध्वम् यथा भागम् आवृषायध्वम् इति ।
2.7.m: He should address the presented [balls]: 'Here, O fathers, exhilarate yourselves! Like bulls, each according to his share!'

2.7.s: savya āvṛd udann āvṛtya yathā śakty aprāṇann āsitvā abhiparyāvṛttya amīmadanta pitaro yathā bhāgam āvṛṣāyīṣata iti |
2.7.d: सव्य आवृद् उदन्न् आवृत्य यथा शक्त्य् अप्राणन्न् आसित्वा अभिपर्यावृत्त्य अमीमदन्त पितरो यथा भागम् आवृषायीषत इति ।
2.7.m: Turning to the left towards the north, having remained without breathing as long as he is able, having turned back [towards them, he says]: 'The fathers have exhilarated themselves; like bulls, each according to his share.'

2.7.s: caroḥ prāṇa bhakṣam bhakṣayet |
2.7.d: चरोः प्राण भक्षम् भक्षयेत् ।
2.7.m: He should consume the cooked offering by smelling its breath.

2.7.s: nityam ninayanam |
2.7.d: नित्यम् निनयनम् ।

2.7.s: asāv abhyaṅkṣva asāv aṅkṣva iti piṇḍeṣv abhyañjana añjane |
2.7.d: असाव् अभ्यङ्क्ष्व असाव् अङ्क्ष्व इति पिण्डेष्व् अभ्यञ्जन अञ्जने ।
2.7.m: [He applies] ointment and collyrium to the balls with: 'So-and-so, anoint yourself! So-and-so, apply collyrium!'

2.7.s: vāso dadyād daśām ūrṇā stukā vā pañcāśad varṣatāyā ūrdhvam svam loma etad vaḥ pitaro vāso mā no ato anyat pitaro yuṅgdhvam iti |
2.7.d: वासो दद्याद् दशाम् ऊर्णा स्तुका वा पञ्चाशद् वर्षताया ऊर्ध्वम् स्वम् लोम एतद् वः पितरो वासो मा नो अतो अन्यत् पितरो युङ्ग्ध्वम् इति ।
2.7.m: He should give a garment, the fringe [of a garment], or a tuft of wool, or after the age of fifty years his own body hair, [saying]: 'This is your garment, O fathers; do not equip yourselves with anything else from us, O fathers.'

2.7.s: atha enān upatiṣṭheta namo vaḥ pitara iṣe namo vaḥ pitara ūrje namo vaḥ pitaraḥ śuṣmāya namo vaḥ pitaro aghorāya namo vaḥ pitaro jīvāya namo vaḥ pitaro rasāya | svadhā vaḥ pitaro namo vaḥ pitaro nama etā yuṣmākam pitara imā asmākam jīvā vo jīvanta iha santaḥ syāma |
2.7.d: अथ एनान् उपतिष्ठेत नमो वः पितर इषे नमो वः पितर ऊर्जे नमो वः पितरः शुष्माय नमो वः पितरो अघोराय नमो वः पितरो जीवाय नमो वः पितरो रसाय । स्वधा वः पितरो नमो वः पितरो नम एता युष्माकम् पितर इमा अस्माकम् जीवा वो जीवन्त इह सन्तः स्याम ।
2.7.m: Then he should pay reverence to them: 'Reverence to you, O fathers, for nourishment! Reverence to you, O fathers, for vigor! Reverence to you, O fathers, for fiery energy! Reverence to you, O fathers, for mildness! Reverence to you, O fathers, for life! Reverence to you, O fathers, for sap! Svadhā to you, O fathers! Reverence to you, O fathers, reverence! These are yours, O fathers; these are ours; may we living ones, while living, remain here!'

2.7.s: namo anvāhuvāmaha iti ca tisṛbhiḥ |
2.7.d: नमो अन्वाहुवामह इति च तिसृभिः ।
2.7.m: And with the three [verses beginning]: 'We call reverence after...'

2.7.s: atha enān pravāhayet paretana pitaraḥ somyāso gmbhīrebhiḥ pathibhiḥ pūrviṇebhiḥ | dattāya asmabhyam draviṇe ha bhadram rayim ca naḥ sarva vīram niyacchata iti |
2.7.d: अथ एनान् प्रवाहयेत् परेतन पितरः सोम्यासो ग्म्भीरेभिः पथिभिः पूर्विणेभिः । दत्ताय अस्मभ्यम् द्रविणे ह भद्रम् रयिम् च नः सर्व वीरम् नियच्छत इति ।
2.7.m: Then he should dismiss them: 'Depart, O fathers, who are worthy of Soma, by the deep ancient paths; having given us wealth and prosperity here, grant us heroic descendants with all men!'

2.7.s: agnim pratyetyād agne tam adya aśvam na stomair iti |
2.7.d: अग्निम् प्रत्येत्याद् अग्ने तम् अद्य अश्वम् न स्तोमैर् इति ।
2.7.m: Having approached the fire, he should say: 'O Agni, him today with praises like a horse...'

2.7.s: gārhapatyam yad antarikṣam pṛthivīm uta dyām yan mātaram pitaram jihiṃsima | agnir mā tasmād enaso gārhapatyaḥ pramuñcatu karotu mām anenasam iti |
2.7.d: गार्हपत्यम् यद् अन्तरिक्षम् पृथिवीम् उत द्याम् यन् मातरम् पितरम् जिहिंसिम । अग्निर् मा तस्माद् एनसो गार्हपत्यः प्रमुञ्चतु करोतु माम् अनेनसम् इति ।
2.7.m: [He approaches] the Gārhapatya fire [saying]: 'Whatever harm we have done to the atmosphere, earth, and sky, whatever harm to mother and father, may Agni Gārhapatya release me from that sin; may he make me sinless!'

2.7.s: vīram me datta pitara iti piṇḍānām madhyamam |
2.7.d: वीरम् मे दत्त पितर इति पिण्डानाम् मध्यमम् ।
2.7.m: [Saying]: 'Give me a hero, O fathers,' [he takes] the middle one of the balls.

2.7.s: patnīm prāśayed ādhatta pitaro garbham kumāram puṣkara srajam | yathā ayam arapā asad iti |
2.7.d: पत्नीम् प्राशयेद् आधत्त पितरो गर्भम् कुमारम् पुष्कर स्रजम् । यथा अयम् अरपा असद् इति ।
2.7.m: He should cause his wife to eat it, [saying]: 'Place, O fathers, an embryo, a boy wearing a lotus garland, so that this one may be free from disease!'

2.7.s: apsv itarau |
2.7.d: अप्स्व् इतरौ ।

2.7.s: atipraṇīte vā |
2.7.d: अतिप्रणीते वा ।

2.7.s: yathā vā āgnatur anna kāmyā bhāvaḥ sa prāśnīyāt |
2.7.d: यथा वा आग्नतुर् अन्न काम्या भावः स प्राश्नीयात् ।
2.7.m: Or if he has the condition of desiring food due to illness, he may eat it.

2.7.s: mahā rogeṇa vā abhitaptaḥ prāśnīyād anyatarām gatim gacchati |
2.7.d: महा रोगेण वा अभितप्तः प्राश्नीयाद् अन्यतराम् गतिम् गच्छति ।
2.7.m: Or afflicted with a severe disease he may eat it; he goes to one or the other destiny.

2.7.s: evam anāhita agnir nitye |
2.7.d: एवम् अनाहित अग्निर् नित्ये ।
2.7.m: In this same way one who has not established the fires [performs the rite] on the permanent [domestic fire].

2.7.s: śrapayitvā atipraṇīya juhuyāt |
2.7.d: श्रपयित्वा अतिप्रणीय जुहुयात् ।
2.7.m: Having cooked [the rice] and carried [the fire] forward, he should make the offering.

2.7.s: dvivat pātrāṇām utsargaḥ |
2.7.d: द्विवत् पात्राणाम् उत्सर्गः ।
2.7.m: The disposal of the vessels takes place in pairs.

2.7.s: tṛṇam dvitīyam udrikte |
2.7.d: तृणम् द्वितीयम् उद्रिक्ते ।
2.7.m: A blade of grass is the second [item] when there is an odd number.

2.8.m: Intending to begin the New- and Full-Moon sacrifices, [one performs] the initial introductory sacrifice.

2.8.s: agnā viṣṇū sarasvatī sarasvān agnir bhagī |
2.8.d: अग्ना विष्णू सरस्वती सरस्वान् अग्निर् भगी ।
2.8.m: [The divinities are] Agni-and-Viṣṇu, Sarasvatī, Sarasvant, and Agni Bhagin.

2.8.s: agnā viṣṇū sajoṣase mā vardhantu vā aṅgiraḥ | dyumnair vājebhir āgatam | agnā viṣṇū mahi dhāma priyam vām vītho ghṛtasya guhyā juṣāṇā | dame dame suṣṭutir vām iyānā prati vām jihvā ghṛtam uccaraṇyat | pāvakānaḥ sarasvatī pāvīravī kanyā citrāyuḥ pīpivāṃsam sarasvato divyam suparṇam vāyasam bṛhantam āsavam savitur yathā sa no rādhāṃsy ā bhara iti |
2.8.d: अग्ना विष्णू सजोषसे मा वर्धन्तु वा अङ्गिरः । द्युम्नैर् वाजेभिर् आगतम् । अग्ना विष्णू महि धाम प्रियम् वाम् वीथो घृतस्य गुह्या जुषाणा । दमे दमे सुष्टुतिर् वाम् इयाना प्रति वाम् जिह्वा घृतम् उच्चरण्यत् । पावकानः सरस्वती पावीरवी कन्या चित्रायुः पीपिवांसम् सरस्वतो दिव्यम् सुपर्णम् वायसम् बृहन्तम् आसवम् सवितुर् यथा स नो राधांस्य् आ भर इति ।
2.8.m: 'O Agni-and-Viṣṇu, being of one accord...', 'May these increase you, O Aṅgiras...', 'Come with splendors and prize foods!', 'O Agni-and-Viṣṇu, wide is your dear abode; you two taste the secret ghee, finding pleasure...', 'In every house your beautiful praise goes; towards you may the tongue [of fire] rise up with ghee...', 'Purifying us, Sarasvatī...', 'The maiden of the thunderbolt, whose lifespan is marvelous...', 'The overflowing divine bird of Sarasvant, the great raptor...', 'As the liquor of Savitṛ...', 'So bring us wealth!' [are the formulas].

2.8.s: ādhānād yady āmayāvī yady vā arthā vyatheran puar ādheya iṣṭiḥ |
2.8.d: आधानाद् यद्य् आमयावी यद्य् वा अर्था व्यथेरन् पुअर् आधेय इष्टिः ।
2.8.m: If after the establishment of the fires he is ill, or if his fortunes decline, there is the re-establishment sacrifice.
In it, he should sacrifice the fore-offerings and after-offerings with the case-endings.

2.8.s: samidhaḥ samidho agne agna ājyasya vyantu | tanūnapād agnim agna ājyasya vetu | iḷo agninā agna ājyasya vyantu | barhir agnir agna ājyasya vetv iti |
2.8.d: समिधः समिधो अग्ने अग्न आज्यस्य व्यन्तु । तनूनपाद् अग्निम् अग्न आज्यस्य वेतु । इऌओ अग्निना अग्न आज्यस्य व्यन्तु । बर्हिर् अग्निर् अग्न आज्यस्य वेत्व् इति ।
2.8.m: 'May the kindling-sticks, the kindling-sticks of Agni, O Agni, partake of the clarified butter', 'May Tanūnapāt Agni, O Agni, partake of the clarified butter', 'May the refreshments with Agni, O Agni, partake of the clarified butter', 'May the sacrificial grass, Agni, O Agni, partake of the clarified butter' [are the formulas].

2.8.s: samidhā agnim duvasyata ehy ū ṣu bravāṇi ta ity āgneyāv ājya bhāgau |
2.8.d: समिधा अग्निम् दुवस्यत एह्य् ऊ षु ब्रवाणि त इत्य् आग्नेयाव् आज्य भागौ ।
2.8.m: 'Serve Agni with a kindling-stick...' and 'Come indeed, let me speak to you...' are the two clarified butter portions for Agni.
They are called the 'containing intellect' and 'containing the moon-drop' [verses].
Followers of the Anubrāhmaṇa always place the former first.
'O Agni, you purify our life-spans...' is the second.
However, the designation 'sacrificial offering' is always for the latter.

2.8.s: āgneyam haviḥ | adhā hy agne krator bhadrasya ābhiṣ ṭe adya gīrbhir gṛṇanta ebhir no arkair agne tam adya aśvam na stomair iti samyājye | devam barhir agner vasuvane vau dheyasya vetu devo narāśaṃso agnau vasuvane vasu dheyasya vetv iti |
2.8.d: आग्नेयम् हविः । अधा ह्य् अग्ने क्रतोर् भद्रस्य आभिष् टे अद्य गीर्भिर् गृणन्त एभिर् नो अर्कैर् अग्ने तम् अद्य अश्वम् न स्तोमैर् इति सम्याज्ये । देवम् बर्हिर् अग्नेर् वसुवने वौ धेयस्य वेतु देवो नराशंसो अग्नौ वसुवने वसु धेयस्य वेत्व् इति ।
2.8.m:
The sacrificial offering belongs to Agni. 'For indeed, O Agni, of noble purpose...', 'With these songs today, praising you...', 'With these songs of praise, O Agni...', 'O Agni, him today with praises like a horse...' are the two pairs of invitatory and consecratory verses.
'May the divine sacrificial grass of Agni partake for the winning of wealth, for the bestowing of goods', 'May divine Narāśaṃsa in Agni partake for the winning of wealth, for the bestowing of goods.'

2.9.m: The first-fruits sacrifice is of rice, wild millet, and barley.
One should not eat the new grain without having offered the Agnihotra.

2.9.s: yathā varṣasya tṛptaḥ syād atha āgrayaṇena yajeta |
2.9.d: यथा वर्षस्य तृप्तः स्याद् अथ आग्रयणेन यजेत ।
2.9.m: When he is satisfied with the rain, then he should sacrifice with the Āgrayaṇa sacrifice.

2.9.s: api vā devā āhus tṛpto nūnam vasṣasya āgrayaṇena hi yajata iti agni hotrīm vai nānādaitvā tasyāḥ payasā juhuyāt |
2.9.d: अपि वा देवा आहुस् तृप्तो नूनम् वस्षस्य आग्रयणेन हि यजत इति अग्नि होत्रीम् वै नानादैत्वा तस्याः पयसा जुहुयात् ।
2.9.m: Or rather, the gods say: 'He is indeed satisfied with the rain, for he is sacrificing with the Āgrayaṇa sacrifice.' Having fed [the new corn] to the agnihotra cow, he should offer [in the fire] with her milk.
Or the ritual action [may be performed] with barleys.
In the sacrifice of wild rice (śyāmāka), there is a cooked offering to Soma (saumya caru).

2.9.s: soma yās te mayobhuvo yā te dhāmāni divi yā pṛthivyām ity avāntareḷāyā nityam japam uktvā savye pāṇau kṛtvā itareṇa abhimṛśet prajāpataye tvā graham gṛhṇāmi mahyam śriye mahyam yaśase mahyam anna adyāya |
2.9.d: सोम यास् ते मयोभुवो या ते धामानि दिवि या पृथिव्याम् इत्य् अवान्तरेऌआया नित्यम् जपम् उक्त्वा सव्ये पाणौ कृत्वा इतरेण अभिमृशेत् प्रजापतये त्वा ग्रहम् गृह्णामि मह्यम् श्रिये मह्यम् यशसे मह्यम् अन्न अद्याय ।
2.9.m: Having spoken the constant muttered recitation over the intermediate iḷā (avāntareḷā): 'O Soma, those [forms of thine] which are comforting; those abodes of thine in heaven and which are on earth', and having placed [it] in his left hand, he should touch it with the other [hand, saying]: 'For Prajāpati I take thee as a draught, for myself for fortune, for myself for fame, for myself for the eating of food.'

2.9.s: bhadra annaḥ śreyaḥ samanaiṣṭa devās tvayā avasena samaśīmahi tvā | sa no mayobhūḥ piteva āviśa iha śam no bhava dvipade śam catuṣpada iti | prāśya ācamya nābhim ālabheta amo asu prāṇa tad ṛtam bravīmy amā asi sarvān asi praviṣṭaḥ | sa me jarām rogam apanudya śarīrād amā ma edhi māmṛdhāma indra iti |
2.9.d: भद्र अन्नः श्रेयः समनैष्ट देवास् त्वया अवसेन समशीमहि त्वा । स नो मयोभूः पितेव आविश इह शम् नो भव द्विपदे शम् चतुष्पद इति । प्राश्य आचम्य नाभिम् आलभेत अमो असु प्राण तद् ऋतम् ब्रवीम्य् अमा असि सर्वान् असि प्रविष्टः । स मे जराम् रोगम् अपनुद्य शरीराद् अमा म एधि मामृधाम इन्द्र इति ।
2.9.m: 'O gods, you have brought us to better fortune through auspicious food; through thee, [our] sustenance, may we obtain thee. As such, comforting like a father, enter here unto us; be auspicious to our two-footed, auspicious to our four-footed [creatures].' Having eaten and sipped water, he should touch his navel [with the verse]: 'Thou art the breath Amo, that truth I speak; thou art near at hand, thou hast entered all [parts]. Having driven away old age and disease from my body, be near unto me; may we not perish, O Indra.'

2.9.s: etena bhakṣiṇo bhakṣān sarvatra nava bhojane |
2.9.d: एतेन भक्षिणो भक्षान् सर्वत्र नव भोजने ।
2.9.m: With this [formula] those who consume [the portions] should eat their portions everywhere at the eating of new [corn].
Now for the [offerings of] rice and barley, the two inserted verses (dhāyyā) are in the virāj meter.

2.9.s: agni indrāv indra agnī vā viśve devāḥ somo yadi tatra śyāmāko dyāvā pṛthivī |
2.9.d: अग्नि इन्द्राव् इन्द्र अग्नी वा विश्वे देवाः सोमो यदि तत्र श्यामाको द्यावा पृथिवी ।
2.9.m: Agni and Indra, or Indra and Agni, the All-Gods (Viśve Devāḥ), Soma if wild rice is used there, and Heaven and Earth [are the deities].

2.9.s: ā ghā ye agnim indhate sukarmāṇaḥ suruco devayanto viśve devāsa āgata ye ke ca jmā mahino ahimāyā mahī dyauḥ pṛthivī ca naḥ prapūrvaje pitarā navyasībhir iti |
2.9.d: आ घा ये अग्निम् इन्धते सुकर्माणः सुरुचो देवयन्तो विश्वे देवास आगत ये के च ज्मा महिनो अहिमाया मही द्यौः पृथिवी च नः प्रपूर्वजे पितरा नव्यसीभिर् इति ।
2.9.m: 'Those who kindle Agni, performing good deeds, radiant, seeking the gods...' [ṚV 3.26.4]; 'Come, O All-Gods, whoever [ye are] on earth...' [ṚV 10.63.15]; 'Great is heaven and earth for us, born of old, parents with newer [hymns]...' [ṚV 1.159.1].

2.10.m: In the sacrifice for one desiring long life (āyuṣkāmeṣṭi), [the two verses] contain the word 'jīvātu' (sustenance of life).

2.10.s: ā no agne sucetunā tvam soma mahe bhagam ity agnir āyuṣmān indras trātā |
2.10.d: आ नो अग्ने सुचेतुना त्वम् सोम महे भगम् इत्य् अग्निर् आयुष्मान् इन्द्रस् त्राता ।
2.10.m: 'Unto us, O Agni, with good intention...' [ṚV 1.89.1]; 'Thou, O Soma, for great fortune...' [ṚV 1.91.1]—these are for Agni possessing long life (āyuṣmat) and Indra the protector (trātṛ).

2.10.s: āyuṣ ṭe viśvato dadhad ayam agnir vareṇyaḥ | punas te prāṇa āyātu parā yakṣmam suvāmi te | āyurdā agne haviṣo juṣāṇo ghṛta pratīko ghṛta yonir edhi | ghṛtam pītvā madhu cāru gavyam pitā iva putram abhirakṣatād imam | trātāram indram avitāram indram mā te asyām sahasāvan pariṣṭau | pāhi no agne pāyubhir ajasrair agne tvam pārayā navyo asmān iti samyājye |
2.10.d: आयुष् टे विश्वतो दधद् अयम् अग्निर् वरेण्यः । पुनस् ते प्राण आयातु परा यक्ष्मम् सुवामि ते । आयुर्दा अग्ने हविषो जुषाणो घृत प्रतीको घृत योनिर् एधि । घृतम् पीत्वा मधु चारु गव्यम् पिता इव पुत्रम् अभिरक्षताद् इमम् । त्रातारम् इन्द्रम् अवितारम् इन्द्रम् मा ते अस्याम् सहसावन् परिष्टौ । पाहि नो अग्ने पायुभिर् अजस्रैर् अग्ने त्वम् पारया नव्यो अस्मान् इति सम्याज्ये ।
2.10.m:
'Bestowing life upon thee from every side, may this desirable Agni... / May thy breath come back to thee; I drive away consumption from thee. / O Agni, giver of life, enjoying the oblation, with a ghee-face, ghee-wombed be thou. / Drinking the sweet, pleasant ghee of the cow, protect this man like a father his son.'
'Indra the savior, Indra the protector...' [ṚV 6.47.11]; 'Let me not in this thy confinement, O mighty one...' [ṚV 7.19.7]; 'Protect us, O Agni, with unceasing guardians...' [ṚV 6.16.30]; 'O Agni, do thou carry us across renewed...' [ṚV 5.4.9] are the two pairs of consecratory verses (samyājyā).
In the sacrifice for well-being (svastyayanī), [the two verses] contain the word 'rakṣitṛ' (protector).

2.10.s: agne rakṣā no aṃhasas tvam naḥ soma viśvata iti |
2.10.d: अग्ने रक्षा नो अंहसस् त्वम् नः सोम विश्वत इति ।
2.10.m: 'O Agni, protect us from distress...' [ṚV 5.24.1]; 'Thou, O Soma, from all sides for us...' [ṚV 1.91.8].

2.10.s: agniḥ svastimān svasti no divo agne pṛthivyā āre asmad amatim āre aṃha iti pūrvayokte samyājye |
2.10.d: अग्निः स्वस्तिमान् स्वस्ति नो दिवो अग्ने पृथिव्या आरे अस्मद् अमतिम् आरे अंह इति पूर्वयोक्ते सम्याज्ये ।
2.10.m: For Agni possessing well-being (svastimat): 'Well-being for us from heaven, O Agni, [and] from earth...' [ṚV 5.51.11–13]; 'Far from us lack of thought, far distress...' [ṚV 10.77.6]; and the two previously mentioned consecratory verses.
In the sacrifice for one desiring a son (putrakāmeṣṭi), Agni is possessing a son (putrin).

2.10.s: yasmai tvam sukṛte jāta vedo yas tvā hṛdā kīriṇā manyamānaḥ | agnis tu viśravastamam iti dve samyājye |
2.10.d: यस्मै त्वम् सुकृते जात वेदो यस् त्वा हृदा कीरिणा मन्यमानः । अग्निस् तु विश्रवस्तमम् इति द्वे सम्याज्ये ।
2.10.m: 'To whomsoever thou, O Jātavedas, for the well-doer...' [ṚV 5.4.11]; 'He who, O Agni, thinking of thee with a praising heart...' [ṚV 8.84.1]; 'Agni, indeed, the most famous...' [ṚV 5.25.5]—these are two consecratory verses.
The two regular [verses] containing the word 'mūrdhan' ('Agni is the head...' [ṚV 8.44.16] and 'Thou hast become the sacrifice's...' [ṚV 10.8.6]) [are used].

2.10.s: tubhyam tā aṅgirastama aśyāma tam kāmam agne tava iti kāmāya |
2.10.d: तुभ्यम् ता अङ्गिरस्तम अश्याम तम् कामम् अग्ने तव इति कामाय ।
2.10.m: 'Unto thee these, O most Aṅgiras-like...' [ṚV 4.10.1]; 'May we attain that desire, O Agni, of thine...' [ṚV 8.11.9] are for the [attainment of] desire.

2.10.s: vi na indra mṛdho jahi mṛgo na bhīmaḥ kucaro giriṣṭhāḥ | sadyuttim indra sacyutim pracyutim jaghana cyutim | pranākāphāna ābhara prayapsyann iva sakthyau vi na indra mṛdho jahi | canīkhudad yathāsapham abhi naḥ suṣṭutim naya iti |
2.10.d: वि न इन्द्र मृधो जहि मृगो न भीमः कुचरो गिरिष्ठाः । सद्युत्तिम् इन्द्र सच्युतिम् प्रच्युतिम् जघन च्युतिम् । प्रनाकाफान आभर प्रयप्स्यन्न् इव सक्थ्यौ वि न इन्द्र मृधो जहि । चनीखुदद् यथासफम् अभि नः सुष्टुतिम् नय इति ।
2.10.m: 'Dispel, O Indra, our foes, like a terrible wild beast moving at will, living in the mountains...' [ṚV 10.180.2]; 'A swift falling, O Indra, an active falling, a falling forth, a falling of the rump; / bring [it] near, like a bird fluttering its wings, as if about to copulate with the thighs; dispel, O Indra, our foes; / piercing like a hoof, lead our hymn of praise unto us.'
To Indra the giver, or the giver again.

2.10.s: yāni no dhanāni kruddho jināsi manyunā | indra anuviddhi nas tāni anena haviṣā punaḥ | punar na indro maghavā dadātu dhanāni śakro dhanīḥ surādhāḥ | asmadryak kṛṇutām yācito manaḥ śruṣṭī na indro haviṣā mṛdhāti iti |
2.10.d: यानि नो धनानि क्रुद्धो जिनासि मन्युना । इन्द्र अनुविद्धि नस् तानि अनेन हविषा पुनः । पुनर् न इन्द्रो मघवा ददातु धनानि शक्रो धनीः सुराधाः । अस्मद्र्यक् कृणुताम् याचितो मनः श्रुष्टी न इन्द्रो हविषा मृधाति इति ।
2.10.m: 'Whatever riches of ours thou didst take away, angered in wrath, / find them again for us, O Indra, by this oblation. / May Indra Maghavan give us riches again, the powerful one, wealthy, truly liberal; / may he turn his mind toward us when implored; may Indra destroy [the foes] in response to our oblation.'
Or to the quarters, [or] to the guardians of the quarters.

2.10.s: āśānām āśā pālebhyaś caturbhyo amṛtebhyaḥ | idam bhūtasya adhyakṣebhyo vidhema haviṣā vayam | viśvā āśā madhunā saṃsṛjāmi anamīvā āpa oṣadhayaḥ santu sarvāḥ | ayam yajamāno mṛdho vyasyatv agṛbhītāḥ paśavaḥ santu sarva iti |
2.10.d: आशानाम् आशा पालेभ्यश् चतुर्भ्यो अमृतेभ्यः । इदम् भूतस्य अध्यक्षेभ्यो विधेम हविषा वयम् । विश्वा आशा मधुना संसृजामि अनमीवा आप ओषधयः सन्तु सर्वाः । अयम् यजमानो मृधो व्यस्यत्व् अगृभीताः पशवः सन्तु सर्व इति ।
2.10.m: 'To the quarters, to the guardians of the quarters, to the four immortals, / to these superintendents of creation, let us worship with oblation. / I unite all quarters with sweetness; let waters, let all plants be free from disease; / may this sacrificer cast away foes; may all cattle be unseized.'
Earth, Intermediate Space, and Heaven are the deities.

2.10.s: pṛthivīm mātaram mahīm antarikṣam upabruve | bṛhatīm ūtaye divam | viśvam bibharti pṛthivī antarikṣam vipaprathe | duhe dyaur bṛhatī payaḥ | varma me pṛthivī mahī antarikṣam svastaye | dyaur me śarma mahi śrava iti tisras trayāṇām |
2.10.d: पृथिवीम् मातरम् महीम् अन्तरिक्षम् उपब्रुवे । बृहतीम् ऊतये दिवम् । विश्वम् बिभर्ति पृथिवी अन्तरिक्षम् विपप्रथे । दुहे द्यौर् बृहती पयः । वर्म मे पृथिवी मही अन्तरिक्षम् स्वस्तये । द्यौर् मे शर्म महि श्रव इति तिस्रस् त्रयाणाम् ।
2.10.m: 'Earth the great mother, the Intermediate Space I invoke, and high Heaven for aid. / Earth bears all, Intermediate Space has expanded, high Heaven yields milk. / Earth the great is my armor, Intermediate Space for my well-being, Heaven is my refuge, great fame'—these are three [verses] for the three [deities].
The first two [quarters] are for the first, [the middle two for the second], and the last two for the middle one.

2.11.m: The Mitravindā [sacrifice] has the Great Vairāja ritual framework.

2.11.s: agniḥ somo varuṇo mitra indro bṛhaspatiḥ savitā pūṣā sarasvatī tvaṣṭā ity eka pradānāḥ |
2.11.d: अग्निः सोमो वरुणो मित्र इन्द्रो बृहस्पतिः सविता पूषा सरस्वती त्वष्टा इत्य् एक प्रदानाः ।
2.11.m: Agni, Soma, Varuṇa, Mitra, Indra, Bṛhaspati, Savitṛ, Pūṣan, Sarasvatī, and Tvaṣṭṛ receive a single joint offering.

2.11.s: agniḥ somo varuṇo mitra indro bṛhaspatiḥ savitā yaḥ sahasrī | pūṣā no gobhir avasā sarasvatī tvaṣṭā rūpeṇa samanaktu yajñam |
2.11.d: अग्निः सोमो वरुणो मित्र इन्द्रो बृहस्पतिः सविता यः सहस्री । पूषा नो गोभिर् अवसा सरस्वती त्वष्टा रूपेण समनक्तु यज्ञम् ।
2.11.m: 'Agni, Soma, Varuṇa, Mitra, Indra, Bṛhaspati, Savitṛ who possesses thousands, / Pūṣan with cattle for our aid, Sarasvatī, and Tvaṣṭṛ, may he adorn the sacrifice with form.'

2.11.s: pratilomam ādiśya yajad ye yajāmahe tvaṣṭāram sarasvatīm pūṣaṇam savitāram bṛhaspatim indram mitram varuṇam somam agnim tvaṣṭā rūpāṇi dadhatī sarasvatī bhagam pūṣā savitā no dadātu | bṛhaspatir dadad indraḥ sahasram mitro dātā varuṇaḥ somo agnir iti |
2.11.d: प्रतिलोमम् आदिश्य यजद् ये यजामहे त्वष्टारम् सरस्वतीम् पूषणम् सवितारम् बृहस्पतिम् इन्द्रम् मित्रम् वरुणम् सोमम् अग्निम् त्वष्टा रूपाणि दधती सरस्वती भगम् पूषा सविता नो ददातु । बृहस्पतिर् ददद् इन्द्रः सहस्रम् मित्रो दाता वरुणः सोमो अग्निर् इति ।
2.11.m: Naming [them] in reverse order, he should recite the consecratory verse: 'We who sacrifice unto Tvaṣṭṛ, Sarasvatī, Pūṣan, Savitṛ, Bṛhaspati, Indra, Mitra, Varuṇa, Soma, and Agni: may Tvaṣṭṛ conferring forms, Sarasvatī, Pūṣan, and Savitṛ give us fortune; / may Bṛhaspati give, may Indra [give] a thousand, Mitra the giver, Varuṇa, Soma, and Agni.'
There are eight [sacrifices] having the Vairāja ritual framework.
The first six among them have a single oblation.
One performing sorcery (abhicaran) should sacrifice with the Snuṣāśvaśurīyā sacrifice.

2.11.s: indraḥ sūro atarad rajāṃsi snuṣā sapatnā śvaśuro aham asmi | aham śatrūn jayāmi jarhṛṣāṇo aham vājam jayāmi vāja sātau | indraḥ sūraḥ prathamo viśva karmā marutvān astu gaṇavān sujātaiḥ | mama snuṣā śvaśurasya praviṣṭau sapatnā vācam manasa upāsatām |
2.11.d: इन्द्रः सूरो अतरद् रजांसि स्नुषा सपत्ना श्वशुरो अहम् अस्मि । अहम् शत्रून् जयामि जर्हृषाणो अहम् वाजम् जयामि वाज सातौ । इन्द्रः सूरः प्रथमो विश्व कर्मा मरुत्वान् अस्तु गणवान् सुजातैः । मम स्नुषा श्वशुरस्य प्रविष्टौ सपत्ना वाचम् मनस उपासताम् ।
2.11.m: "Indra, the hero, crossed the spaces; my rival is the daughter-in-law, I am the father-in-law. / Rejoicing, I conquer enemies; I win the prize in the winning of the prize. / May Indra, the hero, the foremost, the all-maker, accompanied by the Maruts, be attended by hosts of noble birth. / Let the rival daughter-in-law, entered into the presence of my father-in-law, attend upon [my] speech with her mind."

2.11.s: joṣṭo damūnā agne śardha mahate saubhagāya iti samyājye |
2.11.d: जोष्टो दमूना अग्ने शर्ध महते सौभगाय इति सम्याज्ये ।
2.11.m: "Cherished, household [Agni]" [and] "O Agni, give strength for great good fortune" are the two samyājyā verses.
For the sake of agreement among those who disagree, the Saṃjñānī sacrifice [is performed].

2.11.s: agnir vasumān somo rudravān indro marutvān varuṇa ādityavān ity eka pradānāḥ |
2.11.d: अग्निर् वसुमान् सोमो रुद्रवान् इन्द्रो मरुत्वान् वरुण आदित्यवान् इत्य् एक प्रदानाः ।
2.11.m: Agni with the Vasus, Soma with the Rudras, Indra with the Maruts, [and] Varuṇa with the Ādityas share a single offering.

2.11.s: agniḥ prathamo vasubhir no avyāt somo rudrair abhirakṣatu tmanā | indro marudbhir ṛtuthā kṛṇotu ādityair no varuṇaḥ śarma yaṃsat | sam agnir vasubhir no avyāt sam somo rudriyābhis tanūbhiḥ | sam indro rāta havyo marudbhiḥ sam ādityair varuṇo viśva vedā iti |
2.11.d: अग्निः प्रथमो वसुभिर् नो अव्यात् सोमो रुद्रैर् अभिरक्षतु त्मना । इन्द्रो मरुद्भिर् ऋतुथा कृणोतु आदित्यैर् नो वरुणः शर्म यंसत् । सम् अग्निर् वसुभिर् नो अव्यात् सम् सोमो रुद्रियाभिस् तनूभिः । सम् इन्द्रो रात हव्यो मरुद्भिः सम् आदित्यैर् वरुणो विश्व वेदा इति ।
2.11.m: "May Agni as foremost protect us with the Vasus, may Soma with the Rudras guard [us] himself; / may Indra with the Maruts act in season, may Varuṇa with the Ādityas grant us protection. / May Agni with the Vasus favour us, may Soma with his Rudrian forms [favour us]; / may Indra, to whom offerings are made, [favour us] with the Maruts, and all-knowing Varuṇa with the Ādityas."
Those desiring division [perform the sacrifice] to Indra and the Maruts.

2.11.s: maruto yasya hi kṣaye praśardhāya mārutāya svabhānava iti |
2.11.d: मरुतो यस्य हि क्षये प्रशर्धाय मारुताय स्वभानव इति ।
2.11.m: "In whose dwelling the Maruts [drink]" [and] "To the host of Maruts, self-luminous..." [are the verses].

2.11.s: aindrīm anūcya mārutyā yajen mārutīm anūcya aindryā yajed indram pūrvam nigameṣu maruto vā |
2.11.d: ऐन्द्रीम् अनूच्य मारुत्या यजेन् मारुतीम् अनूच्य ऐन्द्र्या यजेद् इन्द्रम् पूर्वम् निगमेषु मरुतो वा ।
2.11.m: Having recited the introductory verse to Indra, he should offer the consecratory verse to the Maruts; having recited the introductory verse to the Maruts, he should offer the consecratory verse to Indra; or Indra [may be named] first in the formulas, or the Maruts.
Or Indra [is placed first]; after the principal offering, the Maruts [are named].
Those desiring agreement [perform the sacrifice] in its archetypal form, and also the Saṃjñānī sacrifice.
Those being attacked [perform the sacrifice] to Indra and Bṛhaspati.

2.11.s: ā na indrā bṛhaspatī asmai indrā bṛhaspatī iti yady api indrāya codayeyuḥ |
2.11.d: आ न इन्द्रा बृहस्पती अस्मै इन्द्रा बृहस्पती इति यद्य् अपि इन्द्राय चोदयेयुः ।
2.11.m: "To us, O Indra and Bṛhaspati" [and] "To him, O Indra and Bṛhaspati...", even if they should designate it for Indra.

2.12.s: apām idma nyayanam samudrasya niveśanam | anyante asmat tapantu hetayaḥ pāvako asmabhyam śivo bhava | namas te harase śociṣe namas te astv arciṣe | anyante asmat tapantu hetayaḥ pāvako asmabhyam śivo bhava iti pāvakavatyo dhāyye |
2.12.d: अपाम् इद्म न्ययनम् समुद्रस्य निवेशनम् । अन्यन्ते अस्मत् तपन्तु हेतयः पावको अस्मभ्यम् शिवो भव । नमस् ते हरसे शोचिषे नमस् ते अस्त्व् अर्चिषे । अन्यन्ते अस्मत् तपन्तु हेतयः पावको अस्मभ्यम् शिवो भव इति पावकवत्यो धाय्ये ।
2.12.m: "This is the descending-place of the waters, the dwelling of the sea; / let your missiles burn another than us; O Purifier, be auspicious to us. / Homage to your fury, to your blazing heat, homage be to your flame; / let your missiles burn another than us; O Purifier, be auspicious to us"—these are the two purifying inserted verses.
The two clarified butter portions are provided with [verses mentioning] "the purifier" (pāvaka).
[and] "Who with a purifying stream..." [is the other].

2.12.s: yat te pavitram arciṣy ā kalaśeṣu dhāvati iti |
2.12.d: यत् ते पवित्रम् अर्चिष्य् आ कलशेषु धावति इति ।
2.12.m: "That filter of yours in the flame" [and] "Runs into the jars..."

2.12.s: agniḥ pavamānaḥ sarasvatī priyā agniḥ pāvakaḥ savitā satya prasavo agniḥ śucir vāyur niyutvān agnir vrata patir dadhikrāvā agnir vaiśvānaro viṣṇuḥ śipiviṣṭaḥ |
2.12.d: अग्निः पवमानः सरस्वती प्रिया अग्निः पावकः सविता सत्य प्रसवो अग्निः शुचिर् वायुर् नियुत्वान् अग्निर् व्रत पतिर् दधिक्रावा अग्निर् वैश्वानरो विष्णुः शिपिविष्टः ।
2.12.m: [The deities are:] Agni Pavamāna, Sarasvatī the Dear, Agni Pāvaka, Savitṛ of True Impulsion, Agni Śuci, Vāyu accompanied by Niyut steeds, Agni Lord of Vows, Dadhikrāvā, Agni Vaiśvānara, [and] Viṣṇu Śipiviṣṭa.

2.12.s: uta naḥ priya apriyāsv imā juhvānā yuṣmad ā namobhiḥ |
2.12.d: उत नः प्रिय अप्रियास्व् इमा जुह्वाना युष्मद् आ नमोभिः ।
2.12.m: "And to us, dear among the dear ones..." [and] "These being offered to you with homages..." [are the verses for Sarasvatī].

2.12.s: vāyur agregā yajñaprīr vāyo śukro ayāmi te |
2.12.d: वायुर् अग्रेगा यज्ञप्रीर् वायो शुक्रो अयामि ते ।
2.12.m: "Vāyu goes in front, pleasing the sacrifice..." [and] "O Vāyu, the bright [Soma] has been offered to you..." [are for Vāyu].

2.12.s: dadhikrāvṇo akāriṣam ādadhikrāḥ śavasā pañca kṛṣṭīḥ |
2.12.d: दधिक्राव्णो अकारिषम् आदधिक्राः शवसा पञ्च कृष्टीः ।
2.12.m: "I have sung the praise of Dadhikrāvā..." [and] "Dadhikrā has extended over the five peoples with might..." [are for Dadhikrāvā].

2.12.s: juṣṭo damūnā agne śardha mahate saubhagāya iti samyājye |
2.12.d: जुष्टो दमूना अग्ने शर्ध महते सौभगाय इति सम्याज्ये ।
2.12.m: "Cherished, household [Agni]" [and] "O Agni, give strength for great good fortune" are the two samyājyā verses.
This [sacrifice is performed] for one who has resided away for more than a year,

2.12.s: tad eṣā abhi yajña gāthā gīyate | vaiśvānarīm vrātapatīm pavitra iṣṭim tathaiva ca | ṛtāvṛdhau prayuñjānaḥ punāti daśa pauruṣam iti |
2.12.d: तद् एषा अभि यज्ञ गाथा गीयते । वैश्वानरीम् व्रातपतीम् पवित्र इष्टिम् तथैव च । ऋतावृधौ प्रयुञ्जानः पुनाति दश पौरुषम् इति ।
2.12.m: Regarding this, the sacrificial verse is sung: / "Performing the [sacrifice] to Vaiśvānara, the one to the Lord of Vows, and likewise the Pavitreṣṭi, / increasing cosmic order at the turn of the seasons, he purifies ten generations."

2.13.m: The sacrifice for one desiring rain is the Kārīrī.

2.13.s: tasyām prati tyam cārum adhvaram īḷe agnim svavasam namobhir iti dhāyye |
2.13.d: तस्याम् प्रति त्यम् चारुम् अध्वरम् ईऌए अग्निम् स्ववसम् नमोभिर् इति धाय्ये ।
2.13.m: In it, "Towards that lovely sacrifice..." [and] "I praise Agni who provides good aid with homages..." are the two inserted verses.

2.13.s: yāḥ kāś ca varṣa kāma iṣṭyā apsumantau |
2.13.d: याः काश् च वर्ष काम इष्ट्या अप्सुमन्तौ ।
2.13.m: In whatever sacrifices are for one desiring rain, the two [clarified butter portions] contain [verses mentioning] "water" (apsumant).

2.13.s: apsv agne sadhiṣ ṭava apsu me somo abravīd iti |
2.13.d: अप्स्व् अग्ने सधिष् टव अप्सु मे सोमो अब्रवीद् इति ।
2.13.m: "In the waters, O Agni, is your seat" [and] "Soma told me: in the waters..." [are the verses].
[The deities are:] Agni Dhāmacchad, the Maruts, [and] Sūrya.
And the subsequent three lump-offerings [piṇḍīs are made].

2.13.s: hiraṇya keśo rajaso visāra iti dve tvam tyā cid acyutā dhāmante viśvam bhuvanam adhiśritam iti vā vāśreva vidyun mimāti parvataś cin mahi vṛddho bibhāya sṛjanti raśmim ojasā vahiṣṭhebhir viharan yāsi tantum udīrayathā marutaḥ samudrataḥ pra vo marutas taviṣā udanyava āyam naraḥ sudānavo dadāśuṣe vidyun mahaso naro aśmadidyavaḥ kṛṣṇam niyānam harayaḥ suparṇā niyutvanto grāmajito yathā naraḥ |
2.13.d: हिरण्य केशो रजसो विसार इति द्वे त्वम् त्या चिद् अच्युता धामन्ते विश्वम् भुवनम् अधिश्रितम् इति वा वाश्रेव विद्युन् मिमाति पर्वतश् चिन् महि वृद्धो बिभाय सृजन्ति रश्मिम् ओजसा वहिष्ठेभिर् विहरन् यासि तन्तुम् उदीरयथा मरुतः समुद्रतः प्र वो मरुतस् तविषा उदन्यव आयम् नरः सुदानवो ददाशुषे विद्युन् महसो नरो अश्मदिद्यवः कृष्णम् नियानम् हरयः सुपर्णा नियुत्वन्तो ग्रामजितो यथा नरः ।
2.13.m: "Golden-haired, spreading through the mist..." are two verses; or "You, even those unshakeable ones..." [and] "In your abode the whole world rests"; "The lightning bellows like a lowing cow"; "Even the mighty mountain was afraid"; "They release the stream by their power"; "Traversing with the swiftest steeds, you go along the thread"; "Raise up [the rain], O Maruts, from the ocean"; "Forth, O Maruts, mighty, longing for water"; "To the generous donor come these men of bountiful gifts"; "Men possessing the might of lightning, armed with stone missiles"; "A dark pathway, the golden eagles"; "Having teams of horses, conquering settlements like men..."

2.13.s: agne bādhasva vimṛdho vidur grahā yam tvā devāpiḥ śuśucāno agna iti samyājye | ṛco anūcya yajurbhir eke yajanti |
2.13.d: अग्ने बाधस्व विमृधो विदुर् ग्रहा यम् त्वा देवापिः शुशुचानो अग्न इति सम्याज्ये । ऋचो अनूच्य यजुर्भिर् एके यजन्ति ।
2.13.m: "O Agni, repel the hostile forces..." [and] "Which [offering] the glowing Devāpi [made] to you, O Agni..." are the two samyājyā verses. Having recited the verses, some make the offering with the sacrificial formulas.

2.13.s: saṃsthitāyām sarvā diśa upatiṣṭheta achā vada tavasam gīrbhir ābhir iti catasṛbhiḥ pratyṛcam sūktena sūktena vā |
2.13.d: संस्थितायाम् सर्वा दिश उपतिष्ठेत अछा वद तवसम् गीर्भिर् आभिर् इति चतसृभिः प्रत्यृचम् सूक्तेन सूक्तेन वा ।
2.13.m: When it is concluded, he should worship all the directions with the four verses beginning: "Speak forth to the mighty one with these songs...", verse by verse, or hymn by hymn.

2.14.m: Henceforth are the sessions of sacrifices (iṣṭy-ayanas).

2.14.s: teṣām phālgunyām paurṇamāsyām caitryām vā prayogaḥ |
2.14.d: तेषाम् फाल्गुन्याम् पौर्णमास्याम् चैत्र्याम् वा प्रयोगः ।
2.14.m: Their performance begins on the full-moon day of Phālguna or of Caitra.

2.14.s: agnir indro viśve devā iti pṛthag iṣṭayo anusavanam ahar ahaḥ |
2.14.d: अग्निर् इन्द्रो विश्वे देवा इति पृथग् इष्टयो अनुसवनम् अहर् अहः ।
2.14.m: Day after day at each pressing [time, there are] separate sacrifices to Agni, Indra, [and] the Viśve Devas;

2.14.s: dākṣāyaṇa yajñe dve paurṇamāsyau dve amāvāsye yajeta |
2.14.d: दाक्षायण यज्ञे द्वे पौर्णमास्यौ द्वे अमावास्ये यजेत ।
2.14.m: In the Dākṣāyaṇa sacrifice, he should perform two full-moon sacrifices and two new-moon sacrifices.
The two regular [sacrifices] are the former ones, as for one who does not perform the milk-offering (sāṃnāyya) at the new-moon sacrifice.
Of the two latter ones, the second [offering] at the full-moon sacrifice is to Indra;
[and] to Mitra-Varuṇa at the new-moon sacrifice.

2.14.s: ā no mitrā varuṇā yad baṃhiṣṭham nātividhe sudānū iti prājāpatya iḷād adhaḥ |
2.14.d: आ नो मित्रा वरुणा यद् बंहिष्ठम् नातिविधे सुदानू इति प्राजापत्य इऌआद् अधः ।
2.14.m: "To us, O Mitra and Varuṇa..." [and] "What is most solid..." are [the verses for the offering to Mitra-Varuṇa]; [the offering] to Prajāpati is below the Iḷā [invocation].

2.14.s: prajāpate na tvad etāny anyas tava ime lokāḥ pradiśo diśaś ca parāvato nivata udvataś ca | prajāpate viśvasṛj jīva dhanya idam no deva pratiharya havyam iti dyāvā pṛthivyor ayanam |
2.14.d: प्रजापते न त्वद् एतान्य् अन्यस् तव इमे लोकाः प्रदिशो दिशश् च परावतो निवत उद्वतश् च । प्रजापते विश्वसृज् जीव धन्य इदम् नो देव प्रतिहर्य हव्यम् इति द्यावा पृथिव्योर् अयनम् ।
2.14.m: "O Prajāpati, none other than you... / These worlds are yours, the quarters and intermediate directions, distances, lowlands, and highlands; / O Prajāpati, creator of all, blessed with life, accept this our oblation, O god"—[these verses are used in] the Course of Heaven and Earth.

2.14.s: paurṇamāsena amāvāsyād ā amāvāsyena ā apurṇamāsāt |
2.14.d: पौर्णमासेन अमावास्याद् आ अमावास्येन आ अपुर्णमासात् ।
2.14.m: With the full-moon ritual from [one] new-moon sacrifice; with the new-moon ritual up to [the next] full-moon sacrifice.
In the case of [sacrifices] not traditionally taught, modification of the ritual framework is made according to the purpose.
Or as the Adhvaryu priest may remember.
However, at the churning of fire, [the verses are] in the Vairāja [metre].
The consecratory and introductory verses have the deity as their distinguishing mark.

2.14.s: gāyatry āvatī hūtavaty upoktavatī purastāl lakṣaṇā anuvākyā |
2.14.d: गायत्र्य् आवती हूतवत्य् उपोक्तवती पुरस्ताल् लक्षणा अनुवाक्या ।
2.14.m: An introductory verse is in the Gāyatrī metre, contains a form of the root *av* [“to favour”], contains a form of the root *hū* [“to invoke”], contains a form of *upa* + *vac* [“to address”], and has its distinguishing mark at the beginning.

2.14.s: triṣṭubvatī vītavatī juṣṭavaty upariṣṭāl lakṣaṇā yājyā | api vā anyasya chandasaḥ |
2.14.d: त्रिष्टुब्वती वीतवती जुष्टवत्य् उपरिष्टाल् लक्षणा याज्या । अपि वा अन्यस्य छन्दसः ।
2.14.m: A consecratory verse is in the Triṣṭubh metre, contains a form of the root *vī* [“to enjoy”], contains a form of the root *juṣ* [“to relish”], and has its distinguishing mark at the end; or it may belong to another metre.
However, the consecratory verse should not be shorter [in metre than the introductory verse].

2.14.s: kṣāma naṣṭa hata dagdhavatīs tu varjayet |
2.14.d: क्षाम नष्ट हत दग्धवतीस् तु वर्जयेत् ।
2.14.m: One should avoid [verses] containing [words meaning] emaciated, lost, struck down, or burnt.
When the deity is explicitly mentioned, however, [the rule applies] just so.
Or the characteristic mark [may be used] even when [the deity is] unexpressed.
If one does not find [suitable verses] at all,
[one should use] the two Āgneya verses for non-finding;
Having designated the deity, he should utter the praṇava and offer the consecratory verse;

2.14.s: imam ā śṛṇudhī havam yam tvā gīrbhir havāmahe | ā idam barhir niṣīda naḥ | stīrṇam barhir ānuṣag āsad etad upa iḷānā iha no adya gaccha | aheḷatā manasā idam juṣasva vīhi havyam prayatam āhutam ma iti naṃre |
2.14.d: इमम् आ शृणुधी हवम् यम् त्वा गीर्भिर् हवामहे । आ इदम् बर्हिर् निषीद नः । स्तीर्णम् बर्हिर् आनुषग् आसद् एतद् उप इऌआना इह नो अद्य गच्छ । अहेऌअता मनसा इदम् जुषस्व वीहि हव्यम् प्रयतम् आहुतम् म इति नंरे ।
2.14.m: “Hear this our call, you whom we call with songs; sit down upon this barhis of ours; / The barhis is spread continuously to sit on; come here to us today enjoying the invocation; relishing this with an unangered mind, enjoy the offering presented and sacrificed to me”—these are the two Naṃrā verses.
[These] two Āgneya verses are unexpressed [in their deity].

2.15.s: cāturmāsyāni prayokṣyamāṇaḥ pūrve dyur vaiśvānara pārjanyām |
2.15.d: चातुर्मास्यानि प्रयोक्ष्यमाणः पूर्वे द्युर् वैश्वानर पार्जन्याम् ।
2.15.m: One who is about to perform the Cāturmāsya sacrifices [offers] the Vaiśvānara-Pārjanyā [offering] on the preceding day.

2.15.s: vaiśvānaro ajījanad agnir no navyasīm matim | kṣamayā vṛdhāna ojasā | pṛṣṭo divi pṛṣṭo agniḥ pṛthivyām parjanyāya pragāyata pravātā vānti patayanti vidyuta ity agny ādheya prabhṛty antā upāṃśu haviṣaḥ |
2.15.d: वैश्वानरो अजीजनद् अग्निर् नो नव्यसीम् मतिम् । क्षमया वृधान ओजसा । पृष्टो दिवि पृष्टो अग्निः पृथिव्याम् पर्जन्याय प्रगायत प्रवाता वान्ति पतयन्ति विद्युत इत्य् अग्न्य् आधेय प्रभृत्य् अन्ता उपांशु हविषः ।
2.15.m: “Vaiśvānara has begotten; Agni, [bring] to us a newest thought, waxing in might along the earth; / Questioned in heaven, questioned on earth is Agni; sing forth to Parjanya; the forward winds blow, the lightnings fall”—[these are the verses;] ending with the establishment of the sacred fires, the havis offerings are inaudible.
everywhere, with the exception of the offering to Varuṇa.
[And with the exception of] that to Savitṛ in the Cāturmāsyas.
And some [say that] the principal havis offerings [are also inaudible].
The Upasad offerings to the Ancestors have a common ritual framework.
And the ritual of the re-establishment of the sacred fires [is performed inaudibly] prior to the last after-offering (anuyāja);
or rather, their ritual framework is in a very low tone.

2.15.s: āguḥ praṇava vaṣaṭ kārā uccaiḥ sarvatra |
2.15.d: आगुः प्रणव वषट् कारा उच्चैः सर्वत्र ।
2.15.m: The invocation call (āguḥ), the praṇava, and the vaṣaṭ-call are loud everywhere.
Likewise, in the first-fruits offering (āgrayaṇa), the foremost offering [has loud calls].

2.15.s: āhāryas tu prāṇa saṃtataḥ praṇavaḥ puronuvākhyāyāḥ |
2.15.d: आहार्यस् तु प्राण संततः प्रणवः पुरोनुवाख्यायाः ।
2.15.m: However, the praṇava of the introductory verse, continued in one breath, is to be drawn in.
Likewise, the invocation call and the vaṣaṭ-call of the consecratory verse.
The tones of the ritual framework for inaudible [rites] are loud;
those of inaudible ritual frameworks are low-toned.

2.16.s: prātar vaiśvadevyām preṣito agni manthanīyā anvāha paścāt sāmidhenī sthānasya pada mātre avasthāya abhihiṃkṛtya |
2.16.d: प्रातर् वैश्वदेव्याम् प्रेषितो अग्नि मन्थनीया अन्वाह पश्चात् सामिधेनी स्थानस्य पद मात्रे अवस्थाय अभिहिंकृत्य ।
2.16.m: In the morning, at the Vaiśvadeva sacrifice, when summoned, he recites the verses for the churning of fire, having stood a pace behind the place of the kindling verses and having uttered the preliminary sound ‘him’:

2.16.s: abhi tvā deva savitar mahī dyauḥ pṛthivī ca nas tvām agne puṣkarād adhi iti tisṝṇām ardharcam śiṣṭvā āramed ā sampraiṣāt |
2.16.d: अभि त्वा देव सवितर् मही द्यौः पृथिवी च नस् त्वाम् अग्ने पुष्कराद् अधि इति तिसॄणाम् अर्धर्चम् शिष्ट्वा आरमेद् आ सम्प्रैषात् ।
2.16.m: “Unto you, divine Savitṛ…”, “Great heaven and earth to us…”, “You, Agni, from the lotus leaf…”; having left over a half-verse of the three, he should pause until the instruction.

2.16.s: anyatra apy antarṛco avasāne ajāyamāne tv etasminn eva avasāne |
2.16.d: अन्यत्र अप्य् अन्तरृचो अवसाने अजायमाने त्व् एतस्मिन्न् एव अवसाने ।
2.16.m: Elsewhere also, [one pauses] at the pause between verses; if [the fire] is not being generated, however, [he pauses] at this very pause.

2.16.s: agne haṃsi ny atriṇam iti sūktam āvapeta punaḥ punar ājanmanaḥ |
2.16.d: अग्ने हंसि न्य् अत्रिणम् इति सूक्तम् आवपेत पुनः पुनर् आजन्मनः ।
2.16.m: He should interpolate the hymn “Agni, you strike down the devourer…” repeatedly until [the fire’s] birth.

2.16.s: jātam śrutvā anantarreṇa praṇavena śiṣṭam upasaṃtanuyāt |
2.16.d: जातम् श्रुत्वा अनन्तर्रेण प्रणवेन शिष्टम् उपसंतनुयात् ।
2.16.m: Having heard that it is born, he should join what was left over with the immediately preceding praṇava;

2.16.s: śiṣṭena uttarām |
2.16.d: शिष्टेन उत्तराम् ।

2.16.s: uta bruvantu jantava āyam hastena khādinam ity ardharca āramet | pra devam deva vītaya iti dve agninā agniḥ samidhyate tvam hy agne agninā tam arjayanta sukratum yajñena yajñam ayajanta devā iti paridadhyāt |
2.16.d: उत ब्रुवन्तु जन्तव आयम् हस्तेन खादिनम् इत्य् अर्धर्च आरमेत् । प्र देवम् देव वीतय इति द्वे अग्निना अग्निः समिध्यते त्वम् ह्य् अग्ने अग्निना तम् अर्जयन्त सुक्रतुम् यज्ञेन यज्ञम् अयजन्त देवा इति परिदध्यात् ।
2.16.m: “And let the creatures say: ‘He who holds the bracelet in his hand has come’”—at this half-verse he should pause. “Forward the god for the feast of the gods…”—[with these] two [verses], “Agni is kindled by Agni…”, “For you, Agni, by Agni…”, “They acquired him, the wise…”, “With sacrifice the gods sacrificed the sacrifice…” he should conclude.

2.16.s: sarvatra uttamām paridhānīyā iti vidyāt |
2.16.d: सर्वत्र उत्तमाम् परिधानीया इति विद्यात् ।
2.16.m: One should know that everywhere the last verse is the concluding verse.

2.16.s: dhāyye virājau nava prayājāḥ prāg uttamāc catura āvapeta duro agna ājyasya vyantu uṣāsā naktā agna ājyasya vītām daivyā hotārā agna ājyasya vītām tisro devīr agna ājyasya vyantv iti |
2.16.d: धाय्ये विराजौ नव प्रयाजाः प्राग् उत्तमाच् चतुर आवपेत दुरो अग्न आज्यस्य व्यन्तु उषासा नक्ता अग्न आज्यस्य वीताम् दैव्या होतारा अग्न आज्यस्य वीताम् तिस्रो देवीर् अग्न आज्यस्य व्यन्त्व् इति ।
2.16.m: There are two Dhāyyā verses, two Virāj verses, and nine fore-offerings (prayājas); prior to the last one, he should interpolate four: “May the doors, O Agni, enjoy the clarified butter; may Dawn and Night, O Agni, enjoy the clarified butter; may the divine Hotṛ priests, O Agni, enjoy the clarified butter; may the three goddesses, O Agni, enjoy the clarified butter.”

2.16.s: agniḥ somaḥ savitā sarasvatī pūṣā marutaḥ svatavaso viśve devā dyāvā pṛthivī |
2.16.d: अग्निः सोमः सविता सरस्वती पूषा मरुतः स्वतवसो विश्वे देवा द्यावा पृथिवी ।
2.16.m: Agni, Soma, Savitṛ, Sarasvatī, Pūṣan, the Maruts of independent might, the All-gods, and Heaven and Earth [are the deities].

2.16.s: ā viśva devam satpatim vāmam adya savitar vāmam u śvaḥ pūṣan tava vrate vayam śukram te anyad yajatam te anyad iheha vaḥ sva tavasaḥ pra citram arkam gṛṇate turāya iti |
2.16.d: आ विश्व देवम् सत्पतिम् वामम् अद्य सवितर् वामम् उ श्वः पूषन् तव व्रते वयम् शुक्रम् ते अन्यद् यजतम् ते अन्यद् इहेह वः स्व तवसः प्र चित्रम् अर्कम् गृणते तुराय इति ।
2.16.m: “To the all-divine protector of the good…”, “What is dear today, Savitṛ, and what is dear tomorrow…”, “Pūṣan, in your service may we…”, “Bright is one [form] of yours, worshipful the other…”, “Here, here, you of independent might…”, “Proclaim a bright chant for the swift singer…” [are the introductory and consecratory verses].

2.16.s: nava anuyājāḥ ṣaḷ ūrdhvam prathamād devīr dvāro vasuvane vasu dheyasya vyantu | devī uṣāsā naktā vasuvane vasu dheyasya vītām | devī joṣṭrī vasuvane vasu dheyasya vītām | devī ūrjāhutī vasuvane vasu dheyasya vītām | devā daivyā hotārā vasuvane vasu dheyasya vītām | devīs tisras tisro devīr vasuvane vasu dheyasya vyantv iti |
2.16.d: नव अनुयाजाः षऌ ऊर्ध्वम् प्रथमाद् देवीर् द्वारो वसुवने वसु धेयस्य व्यन्तु । देवी उषासा नक्ता वसुवने वसु धेयस्य वीताम् । देवी जोष्ट्री वसुवने वसु धेयस्य वीताम् । देवी ऊर्जाहुती वसुवने वसु धेयस्य वीताम् । देवा दैव्या होतारा वसुवने वसु धेयस्य वीताम् । देवीस् तिस्रस् तिस्रो देवीर् वसुवने वसु धेयस्य व्यन्त्व् इति ।
2.16.m: There are nine after-offerings (anuyājas); six after the first: “May the divine doors enjoy [the offering] for the winning of wealth, for the bestowal of wealth; may the divine Dawn and Night enjoy [the offering] for the winning of wealth, for the bestowal of wealth; may the two divine favouring goddesses enjoy [the offering] for the winning of wealth, for the bestowal of wealth; may the two divine invigorating offerings enjoy [the offering] for the winning of wealth, for the bestowal of wealth; may the two divine Hotṛ priests enjoy [the offering] for the winning of wealth, for the bestowal of wealth; may the three divine goddesses enjoy [the offering] for the winning of wealth, for the bestowal of wealth.”

2.16.s: anuyājānām sūkta vākasya śamyu vākasya vā upariṣṭād vājibhyo vājinam anāvāhya ādeśam |
2.16.d: अनुयाजानाम् सूक्त वाकस्य शम्यु वाकस्य वा उपरिष्टाद् वाजिभ्यो वाजिनम् अनावाह्य आदेशम् ।
2.16.m: After the after-offerings, the recitation of the hymns (sūktavāka), or the recitation of the Śaṃyu formula (śaṃyuvāka), without invoking [the gods], the instruction for the offering of whey (vājina) to the Vājins takes place.

2.16.s: śam no bhavantu vājino haveṣu vāje vāje avata vājino na ity ūrdhvajñur anavānam yājyām |
2.16.d: शम् नो भवन्तु वाजिनो हवेषु वाजे वाजे अवत वाजिनो न इत्य् ऊर्ध्वज्ञुर् अनवानम् याज्याम् ।
2.16.m: “May the swift steeds be auspicious to us at our calls…”, “In every prize, you swift ones, protect us…”—with raised knees, in a single breath, [he recites] the consecratory verse.

2.16.s: agne vīhi ity anuvaṣaṭ kāro vājinasya agne vīhi iti vā | yatra kva ca eka sampraiṣe dvau vaṣaṭ kārau samastāv eva tatra dvir anumantrayeta |
2.16.d: अग्ने वीहि इत्य् अनुवषट् कारो वाजिनस्य अग्ने वीहि इति वा । यत्र क्व च एक सम्प्रैषे द्वौ वषट् कारौ समस्ताव् एव तत्र द्विर् अनुमन्त्रयेत ।
2.16.m: “Agni, enjoy!” is the secondary vaṣaṭ-call for the whey, or “Agni, enjoy the whey!”; and wherever there are two vaṣaṭ-calls on a single summons, he should follow them with formulas twice, combined together.

2.16.s: naca āgūr uttarasmin |
2.16.d: नच आगूर् उत्तरस्मिन् ।

2.16.s: vājina bhakṣam iḷām iva pratigṛhya upahavam icchet |
2.16.d: वाजिन भक्षम् इऌआम् इव प्रतिगृह्य उपहवम् इच्छेत् ।
2.16.m: Having accepted the portion of whey like the iḷā, he should request an invitation [to consume it]:

2.16.s: adhvarya upahvayasva brahmann upahvayasva agnīd upahvayasva iti |
2.16.d: अध्वर्य उपह्वयस्व ब्रह्मन्न् उपह्वयस्व अग्नीद् उपह्वयस्व इति ।
2.16.m: “Adhvaryu, invite me! Brahman priest, invite me! Āgnīdhra priest, invite me!”

2.16.s: yan me retaḥ prasicyate yad vā me api gacchati yad vā jāyate punaḥ | tena mā śivam āviśa tena mā vājinam kuru | tasya te vāji pītasya upahūtasya upahūto bhakṣayāmi iti prāṇa bhakṣam bhakṣayet |
2.16.d: यन् मे रेतः प्रसिच्यते यद् वा मे अपि गच्छति यद् वा जायते पुनः । तेन मा शिवम् आविश तेन मा वाजिनम् कुरु । तस्य ते वाजि पीतस्य उपहूतस्य उपहूतो भक्षयामि इति प्राण भक्षम् भक्षयेत् ।
2.16.m: “Whatever semen of mine is discharged, or whatever passes away from me, or whatever is born again, / with that enter me auspiciously, with that make me vigorous; / of that [whey] of yours drunk by the vigorous, invited [by you], being invited I consume”—thus he should consume it by smelling it.

2.16.s: evam adhvaryur brahmā āgnīdhraḥ |
2.16.d: एवम् अध्वर्युर् ब्रह्मा आग्नीध्रः ।
2.16.m: In this way the Adhvaryu, the Brahman priest, and the Āgnīdhra priest [consume it].

2.16.s: yajamānaḥ pratyakṣam itare ca dīkṣitāḥ |
